t.en: The server makes thousands of thumbnails a day, and the cost is the electricity bill. From this level on there is a budget.

t.zh: 计算量按输出的每个像素算：同一个元件放在只有四分之一大的图上，只花四分之一。
t.en: Cost is counted per output pixel: the same part working on a picture a quarter of the size costs a quarter as much.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：还是 32×32 缩成 8×8，计算量不超过 18。要想的问题：大的模糊为什么贵？
t.en: Your task in this level: again shrink 32×32 to 8×8, with a cost of no more than 18. Something to think about: why is a big blur expensive?

brief.zh: 还是 32×32 缩成 8×8，但计算量不能超过 18。在小图上做事比在大图上便宜：图只有四分之一大时，同样的元件只花四分之一。
brief.en: Again shrink 32×32 to 8×8, but the cost must not exceed 18. Working on a small picture is cheaper than on a big one: on a picture a quarter of the size, the same part costs a quarter as much.

hint.zh: 大的模糊很贵。缩小一半以后，图上的一格相当于原来的两格。
hint.en: A big blur is expensive. After halving, one pixel of the picture stands for two of the original.

after.zh: 缩略图服务每天要处理成千上万张照片：先低通再采样防止混叠，一层层缩小省下计算量。作业 1 比较直接卷积、可分离卷积和 FFT 的速度，比的也是同一笔账。
after.en: A thumbnail service handles thousands of photos a day: low-pass before sampling against aliasing, and shrinking level by level to save work. Assignment 1, comparing the speed of direct convolution, separable convolution and the FFT, does the same accounting.

t.zh: 缩略图服务正式上线：相册要 4×4 的小图标，照片里有斑马板、布纹、细条纹和文字。
t.en: The thumbnail service goes live: the album wants 4×4 icons, and the photos include zone plates, fabric, fine stripes and text.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：从 32×32 缩成 4×4，不出莫尔纹，计算量不超过 19。
t.en: Your task in this level: shrink 32×32 to 4×4 with no moiré and a cost of no more than 19.

brief.zh: 相册要给每张照片做 4×4 的小图标：从 32×32 缩成 4×4，斑马板、布纹、文字都不能出莫尔纹，计算量不能超过 19。
brief.en: The photo album wants a 4×4 icon for every photo: shrink 32×32 to 4×4 with no moiré on zone plates, fabric or text, and a cost of no more than 19.

hint.zh: 前三关各管一件事：先模糊再取样、糊多少、在小图上做事更便宜。
hint.en: Each of the last three levels settled one thing: blur before sampling, how much to blur, and working on small pictures being cheaper.

after.zh: 方波只用到奇数频率，振幅按 1、1/3、1/5、1/7 递减。边越陡，需要的高频越多；只到频率 7 的话，陡边旁边总留着一圈小波纹。任何一条曲线都能这样拆成一组波，这就是傅里叶级数。每道正弦波正负抵消，平均是 0，所以不管怎么叠，整行的平均都是中线。
after.en: A square wave uses only odd frequencies, with amplitudes falling as 1, 1/3, 1/5, 1/7. The steeper an edge, the more high frequencies it needs; stop at frequency 7 and a ripple always remains beside the steep edge. Any curve can be split into waves like this: that is the Fourier series. Each sine wave cancels itself out and averages 0, so however they are stacked, the row averages to the middle line.

t.zh: <level-ref to="2-1"></level-ref>的条纹都是一道干净的波。可真实的图里有方块、字母、边缘，没有一样长得像波。把几道不同频率的波加在一起，能拼出什么样的形状？
t.en: <level-ref to="2-1"></level-ref>'s stripes were a single clean wave. But real pictures have squares, letters and edges, and none of them looks like a wave. What shapes can you make by adding waves of different frequencies together?

t.zh: 声音里也有同样的事：钢琴和小提琴弹同一个音，听起来却不同，因为里面混着的高低不同的波，比例不一样。
t.en: Sound works the same way: a piano and a violin playing the same note sound different, because the waves of different pitch mixed in them come in different proportions.

t.zh: 台上频率 1 到 8 各有一道正弦波，就是<part-ref to="wave"></part-ref>元件选 sin 时的样子。每道波只有一个旋钮：它的振幅。
t.en: The bench has a sine wave for each frequency from 1 to 8, just like the <part-ref to="wave"></part-ref> part set to sin. Each wave has one knob: its amplitude.

caption.en: The <part-ref to="wave"></part-ref> part: sin with k = 2

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：调各个频率的振幅，先叠出由两道波组成的目标，再叠出一条接近方波的曲线。要想的问题：光滑的波能拼出一道陡边吗？
t.en: Your task in this level: set the amplitude of each frequency, first to stack up a target made of two waves, then a curve close to a square wave. Something to think about: can smooth waves make a steep edge?

brief.zh: 频率 1 到 8 各有一道正弦波，每道一个振幅旋钮，加起来再放在 0.5 的中线上。先叠出两道波，再叠出一道接近方波的曲线。
brief.en: There is a sine wave for each frequency from 1 to 8, each with an amplitude knob; they are added up on a middle line of 0.5. Stack up two waves first, then a curve close to a square wave.

hint.zh: 先只调频率 1，看误差还剩哪些起伏，再一道道补上去。
hint.en: Set frequency 1 first, see which wiggles are left over, then add waves one at a time.

note.zh: 目标是几道波加起来的。调各个频率的振幅，把你的曲线叠到目标上。
note.en: The target is a few waves added up. Set the amplitude of each frequency to stack your curve onto the target.

win.zh: 这条曲线就是两道波逐点相加：频率 1 给出一个大起伏，频率 3 在上面添了三个小起伏。看下面的平均：叠了波，整行的平均还是 0.5。
win.en: This curve is just two waves added point by point: frequency 1 gives one big swing, and frequency 3 adds three small ones on top. Look at the average below: with the waves stacked on, the row still averages 0.5.

note.zh: 这次的目标是这些波能叠出的最像方波的样子：一半亮、一半暗，中间是陡边。先只调频率 1，看还差哪些起伏，再一道道补上去。
note.en: This time the target is the nearest these waves come to a square wave: half light, half dark, with a steep edge between. Set frequency 1 first, see which wiggles are still missing, then add waves one at a time.

win.zh: 只用到了奇数频率，而且频率越高振幅越小。高频把边拉陡；只到频率 7，陡边旁边还留着一点小波纹。
win.en: Only odd frequencies were needed, and the higher the frequency, the smaller its amplitude. The high frequencies make the edge steep; stopping at 7 still leaves a little ripple beside it.

after.zh: 探针波和曲线逐点相乘再平均，别的频率互相抵消，只留下同一频率那道波振幅的一半，乘 2 就是它的振幅。换一个探针频率，就量另一道波。
after.en: Multiply a probe wave with the curve point by point and average: the other frequencies cancel, leaving half the amplitude of the wave at the probe's frequency, and twice that is its amplitude. Change the probe's frequency to measure another wave.

t.zh: <level-ref to="2-2"></level-ref>的波是你自己叠的，当然知道每道波有多强。反过来，拿到一条已经叠好的曲线，怎么知道里面有多少 k = 3 的波？调音器认出你弹的是哪个音，做的就是这类事。
t.en: In <level-ref to="2-2"></level-ref> you stacked the waves yourself, so you knew how strong each one was. The other way round: given a curve already stacked, how do you find how much k = 3 wave is in it? A tuner recognising which note you play does this kind of thing.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：在台上转动探针的频率，先找出让乘积的平均不为 0 的那一个，再读出混合曲线里一道波的振幅。要想的问题：乘积什么时候会整体偏到一边？
t.en: Your task in this level: turn the probe's frequency on the bench, first to find the one whose product does not average to 0, then to read one wave's amplitude out of a mixed curve. Something to think about: when does the product lean to one side overall?

brief.zh: 输入是一条曲线，探针是一道你选频率的波。两条曲线逐点相乘，台上画出乘积和它的平均。先找出让平均不为 0 的探针，再从一条混合的曲线里读出一道波的振幅。
brief.en: The input is a curve and the probe is a wave whose frequency you choose. The two are multiplied point by point, and the bench draws the product and its average. First find the probe whose average is not 0, then read one wave's amplitude out of a mixed curve.

hint.zh: 乘积整体偏在 0 的上面还是下面？什么时候正负刚好抵消？
hint.en: Does the product sit above or below 0 overall? When do plus and minus cancel exactly?

note.zh: 输入是一道频率不知道的波。转动探针的频率，看下面两条曲线逐点相乘的结果和它的平均。
note.en: The input is a wave of unknown frequency. Turn the probe's frequency and watch the two curves multiplied point by point below, and the product's average.

win.zh: 只有探针和输入的频率相同，乘积才整体偏到一边，平均不为 0；频率对不上时正负抵消，平均是 0。
win.en: Only when the probe has the input's frequency does the product lean to one side, so its average is not 0; when they differ, plus and minus cancel and the average is 0.

note.zh: 输入是几道波混在一起，其中频率 5 那道的振幅是 0.30。用探针读出它：读数是乘积的平均再乘一个数。
note.en: The input is several waves mixed together; the one at frequency 5 has amplitude 0.30. Read it with the probe: the reading is the product's average times a number.

win.zh: 别的频率在平均里都抵消了，只剩频率 5 那道波振幅的一半：cos 自己乘自己，平均是 ½，所以要乘 2。
win.en: The other frequencies all cancel in the average, leaving half the amplitude of the frequency-5 wave: a cos times itself averages ½, so the reading takes a factor of 2.

after.zh: 一个频率要用两个探针去量：cos 量对齐的部分，sin 量错开四分之一周期的部分，√(a² + b²) 合起来就是振幅，不管波错开多少。
after.en: One frequency takes two probes: cos measures the part lined up with it, sin the part a quarter of a cycle off, and √(a² + b²) puts them together into the amplitude, however far the wave is shifted.

t.zh: <level-ref to="2-3"></level-ref>的输入都和探针对得整整齐齐。可真实的曲线里，一道波不一定从最亮处开始，它可能左右错开。
t.en: <level-ref to="2-3"></level-ref>'s inputs all lined up neatly with the probe. In a real curve, though, a wave need not start at its brightest: it may be shifted sideways.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：把输入错开，看探针还量不量得准；再找出一种不管错开多少都读得准的读法。
t.en: Your task in this level: shift the input and see whether the probe still measures it, then find a way of reading that is right however far the wave is shifted.

brief.zh: 输入是一道频率 3 的波，可以左右错开，探针也是频率 3。先看错开以后探针还量不量得准，再找出一种不怕错开的读法。
brief.en: The input is a wave of frequency 3 that can be shifted sideways, and the probe is frequency 3 too. First see whether the probe still measures it once shifted, then find a way of reading that does not mind the shift.

hint.zh: cos 探针量的是和它对齐的那部分。错开四分之一个周期，还剩多少对齐？
hint.en: The cos probe measures the part lined up with it. Shifted by a quarter of a cycle, how much is still lined up?

note.zh: 输入是一道频率 3、振幅 0.30 的波，探针也是频率 3。转动输入错开的角度，看探针的读数（平均 × 2）怎么变，让它读出 0。
note.en: The input is a wave of frequency 3 and amplitude 0.30, and the probe is frequency 3 too. Turn how far the input is shifted, watch how the probe's reading (average × 2) changes, and make it read 0.

win.zh: 错开四分之一个周期，cos 探针就读出 0：它只量得到和自己对齐的那部分。
win.en: Shifted by a quarter of a cycle, the cos probe reads 0: it only measures the part lined up with itself.

status.en: The probe still measures part of it.

note.zh: 现在 sin 探针也打开了，台上同时显示两个读数：cos 的 a 和 sin 的 b。哪种合起来的读法，不管错开多少，都等于这道波的振幅 0.30？
note.en: Now the sin probe is on too, and the bench shows both readings: a from cos and b from sin. Which way of combining them equals the wave's amplitude, 0.30, however far it is shifted?

win.zh: cos 和 sin 各量到一部分：a = A·cos φ，b = A·sin φ。√(a² + b²) 正好是 A，和错开多少无关。
win.en: cos and sin each measure a part: a = A·cos φ and b = A·sin φ. √(a² + b²) is exactly A, however far the wave is shifted.

status.zh: 选一种读法，看看不同角度下它是多少。
status.en: Pick a combination and see what it gives at different angles.

after.zh: 这就是傅里叶变换：拿每个频率的 cos 和 sin 去和信号逐点相乘、求平均。两个读数 a、b 合起来，振幅是 2·√(a² + b²)，和波错开多少无关；错开多少（相位）是 atan2(b, a)。只用 cos 的探针会把错开 90° 的波量成 0。图像也一样，只是波有两个方向：对每一个 (kx, ky) 都做一次探针，把测到的振幅画在 (kx, ky) 那一格，就是图像的频谱，中心是 (0, 0)，也就是平均亮度。
after.en: This is the Fourier transform: multiply the signal per-pixel by the cos and the sin of each frequency, and average. Together the two readings a and b give the amplitude 2·√(a² + b²), however far the wave is shifted; how far it is shifted (the phase) is atan2(b, a). A probe with only cos measures a wave shifted by 90° as 0. Images work the same way, except that waves have two directions: run the probe once for every (kx, ky) and draw the amplitude it measures in cell (kx, ky), and you have the image's spectrum. The centre is (0, 0), the average brightness.

t.zh: <level-ref to="2-3"></level-ref>和<level-ref to="2-4"></level-ref>在台上看过探针怎么工作。这一关要把它搭成电路：输入一条混着几道波、有的还错开的曲线，读出频率 3 那道波的振幅。
t.en: <level-ref to="2-3"></level-ref> and <level-ref to="2-4"></level-ref> showed on the bench how a probe works. This level builds it as a circuit: the input is a curve of several waves mixed, some of them shifted, and you read off the amplitude of the frequency-3 wave.

t.zh: 这一关的电路不处理图像，处理的是一行 32 个点的波形，输出一个数。<part-ref to="mean"></part-ref>把一行数变成一个数。
t.en: This level's circuit does not process an image but a waveform of 32 points, and outputs a single number. <part-ref to="mean"></part-ref> turns a row of numbers into one number.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：读出输入里 k = 3 那道波的振幅，也就是它最亮处比它自己的平均高出多少。五条测试波形都要读准。
t.en: In this level: read off the amplitude of the k = 3 wave in the input, that is, how far its brightest point rises above its own average. Get all five test waveforms right.

caption.zh: 波形 A：输入的一行，和期望读出的数
caption.en: Waveform A: the input row and the expected reading

brief.zh: 输入是一条 32 个点的波形，由几道波和一个平均亮度叠成。读出其中频率 k = 3 那道波的振幅 A，输出一个数。有一条波形里根本没有 k = 3。
brief.en: The input is a waveform of 32 points, made of a few waves plus an average brightness. Read off the amplitude A of the wave with frequency k = 3, and output that one number. One of the waveforms has no k = 3 at all.

hint.zh: 你能自己造一道 k = 3 的波。怎样把它和输入放在一起算，才能让 k = 3 的部分留下、别的频率互相抵消？可藏着的波要是错开了位置呢？
hint.en: You can make a k = 3 wave yourself. How can you combine it with the input so the k = 3 part stays and the other frequencies cancel out? But what if the hidden wave is shifted?

after.zh: 离焦就是模糊，模糊压低了高频。所以频谱外圈越亮，照片越清楚。手机相机对焦时，一边挪镜头一边算这样的分数，停在分数最高的位置。
after.en: Out of focus means blurred, and blurring turns the high frequencies down. So the brighter the outer part of the spectrum, the sharper the photo. A phone camera computes a score like this while it moves the lens, and stops where the score is highest.

t.zh: <level-ref to="2-5"></level-ref>的探针量一行里的一个频率。图像是二维的，波可以横着、竖着、斜着走。对每一种方向和疏密都做一次探针，读数排成一张图，就是<part-ref to="spectrum"></part-ref>：正中心是平均亮度，越往外的格子代表变化越快的波。
t.en: <level-ref to="2-5"></level-ref>'s probe measured one frequency in a row. Images are 2-D, so waves run across, down or at a slant. Run the probe for every direction and density and lay the readings out as a picture, and you have the <part-ref to="spectrum"></part-ref>: the centre is the average brightness, and cells further out stand for faster-changing waves.

caption.zh: 第一组测试照片的频谱
caption.en: The spectrum of the first test photo

t.zh: 相机自动对焦时，要一边挪镜头一边判断：现在这张清楚吗？
t.en: When a camera focuses itself, it moves the lens and keeps asking: is this shot sharp now?

t.zh: 新画法<part-ref to="spectrum"></part-ref>：画出每个频率的波有多强，中心是频率 (0, 0)，越往外频率越高。
t.en: A new way of drawing, <part-ref to="spectrum"></part-ref>: how strong the wave at each frequency is, with frequency (0, 0) at the centre and higher frequencies further out.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：按说明里的规则，给每张照片算一个清晰度分。「频率半径」是一张和频谱一样大的图，每格写着它离中心多远。要想的问题：糊掉的照片，频谱哪里变暗了？
t.en: Your task in this level: score each photo for sharpness by the rule in the brief. "Frequency radius" is a picture the size of the spectrum, each cell holding its distance from the centre. Something to think about: where does the spectrum of a blurred photo get darker?

brief.zh: 相机自动对焦时，要给每一张试拍打一个清晰度分。输出这个分：照片的频谱里，离中心超过 6 的那些格子加起来，再除以频谱的格子总数。「频率半径」告诉你频谱每一格离中心多远。
brief.en: When a camera focuses itself, it scores every trial shot for sharpness. Output that score: the sum of the spectrum cells more than 6 from the centre, divided by the total number of spectrum cells. "Frequency radius" tells you how far each spectrum cell is from the centre.

hint.zh: 先做一张只在半径 6 以外为 1 的图，用它把频谱的内圈遮住。
hint.en: First make a picture that is 1 only beyond radius 6, and use it to mask out the inner part of the spectrum.

after.zh: 空间里的模糊，等于频域里给每个频率乘一个增益，这叫卷积定理。一刀切的增益变回空间，是一个两侧带负瓣的核，边上冒出一圈圈波纹（振铃）；平滑下降的增益几乎没有。高斯增益变回空间还是高斯，期望里的模糊就是它。
after.en: A blur in space equals multiplying every frequency by a gain in the frequency domain: the convolution theorem. A sharp cut-off gain, turned back into space, is a kernel with negative side lobes, so rings appear beside edges (ringing); a gain that falls smoothly has hardly any. A Gaussian gain turned back into space is still a Gaussian, and that is the blur the expected output used.

t.zh: 音响里常有「均衡器」：一排推杆，每根管一段音高，可以把低音推高、把刺耳的高音拉低。图像也可以这样：直接给每个频率调音量，叫增益，1 是原样保留，0 是完全去掉。
t.en: Stereos often have an "equaliser": a row of sliders, each in charge of a range of pitch, so you can push up the bass and pull down a harsh treble. Pictures can be treated the same way: give each frequency a volume, called a gain, where 1 keeps it as it is and 0 removes it entirely.

t.zh: 新元件<part-ref to="part:fqApply"></part-ref>：把图变到频域，每个频率乘上增益图里对应格子的数，再变回来。增益图和频谱的画法一样，中心是频率 (0, 0)。
t.en: The new part <part-ref to="part:fqApply"></part-ref>: takes a picture into the frequency domain, multiplies each frequency by the number in the matching cell of a gain picture, and comes back. The gain picture is laid out like a spectrum, with frequency (0, 0) at the centre.

t.zh: 之前的 3×3 平均、高斯，是在图上让每个像素和邻居混一混。这一关从频率那边下手，结果也是一种模糊。要想的问题：这两种做法是什么关系？
t.en: The 3×3 average and the Gaussian worked on the picture, mixing each pixel with its neighbours. This level works from the frequency side, and the result is a blur too. Something to think about: how are the two approaches related?

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：用「频率半径」做出一张增益图，让输出和期望一样柔和，没有波纹。
t.en: Your task in this level: make a gain picture from "Frequency radius" so the output is as soft as the expected one, with no ripples.

caption.zh: 第一组：带噪点的方块和期望
caption.en: Set 1: a noisy square and the expected output

brief.zh: 期望的输出是一种柔和的模糊，没有任何波纹。这次不在图上模糊，而是到频域里去：给每个频率一个增益，用<part-ref to="part:fqApply"></part-ref>处理照片。增益图要你自己用「频率半径」做出来。
brief.en: The expected output is a soft blur with no ripples at all. This time you do not blur on the picture; you go to the frequency domain instead: give each frequency a gain and process the photo with <part-ref to="part:fqApply"></part-ref>. You make the gain picture yourself, from "Frequency radius".

hint.zh: 低频留下、高频压掉。一刀切的增益会在边旁边留下一圈圈波纹，看误差图。
hint.en: Keep the low frequencies, press down the high ones. A gain that cuts off sharply leaves rings beside the edges: look at the error map.

after.zh: 和<level-ref to="2-7"></level-ref>里一样：硬圆盘一刀切，等于用一个带负瓣的核做卷积，边缘两侧冒出一圈圈亮暗波纹（振铃）；高斯掩膜平滑过渡，对应的核还是高斯，没有波纹。期望图其实是 σ = 1 的空间高斯模糊，对应的掩膜宽度 R = N/(2πσ) = 32/(2π) ≈ 5。空间里卷积，等于频域里相乘，这就是卷积定理。
after.en: Just as in <level-ref to="2-7"></level-ref>: a hard disk cuts sharply, which is the same as a convolution with a kernel that has negative lobes, so rings of light and dark ripple out on both sides of an edge (ringing). A Gaussian mask falls off smoothly; its kernel is still a Gaussian, with no ripples. The expected image is in fact a spatial Gaussian blur with σ = 1, which matches a mask width of R = N/(2πσ) = 32/(2π) ≈ 5. Convolution in space equals multiplication in the frequency domain: this is the convolution theorem.

t.zh: 手机夜景、老照片的扫描件里，常有一层细密的噪点。颗粒越细，变化越快，在频谱上就离中心越远；图里大块的形状变化慢，落在中心附近。
t.en: Night shots on a phone and scans of old photos often have a layer of fine noise. The finer the grain, the faster it changes, and the farther from the centre it sits in the spectrum. Large shapes in the image change slowly and sit near the centre.

caption.zh: 第一组测试输入的频谱
caption.en: Spectrum of the first test input

t.zh: <level-ref to="2-7"></level-ref>搭的东西现在是<part-ref to="freq-filter"></part-ref>元件：以中心为圆心留下一块频率。它有两个设置：掩膜形状（硬圆盘或高斯）和半径 R。<part-ref to="spectrum"></part-ref>元件可以看任何结果的频谱。
t.en: What you built in <level-ref to="2-7"></level-ref> is now the <part-ref to="freq-filter"></part-ref> part: it keeps a disc of frequencies around the centre. It has two settings: the mask shape (hard disc or Gaussian) and the radius R. The <part-ref to="spectrum"></part-ref> part shows the spectrum of any result.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：去掉照片里的噪点，输出要和期望一样干净、柔和。四组测试是方块、圆盘、字母和横条，误差图会告诉你差在哪里。
t.en: In this level: remove the noise from the photos. The output must be as clean and soft as expected. The four test sets are a square, a disc, a letter and horizontal bars; the error map shows you where you are off.

caption.zh: 方块：带噪点的输入和期望
caption.en: Square: the noisy input and the expected output

brief.zh: 照片里混进了细密的噪点。用<part-ref to="freq-filter"></part-ref>去掉它们，输出要和期望一样干净、柔和。
brief.en: Fine noise has crept into the photos. Remove it with <part-ref to="freq-filter"></part-ref>: the output must be as clean and soft as the expected image.

hint.zh: 离频谱中心 R 以内的频率留下，以外压掉。两种掩膜形状，哪种不起波纹？盯住误差图里边缘两侧出现的东西。
hint.en: Frequencies within R of the spectrum's centre stay, and the rest are pressed down. Of the two mask shapes, which makes no ripples? Watch what appears on both sides of the edges in the error map.

after.zh: 一组规则的条纹，在频谱里只占一对点；照片本身的内容散在各处。把那对点挖掉，条纹就没了，照片几乎不受影响。修图软件的「去网纹」、去掉扫描件上的摩尔纹，都是这个办法。
after.en: A regular stripe pattern takes up just one pair of dots in the spectrum, while the photo's own content is spread all over. Dig out that pair and the stripes are gone, with the photo hardly touched. "Descreen" in photo editors, and removing moiré from scans, work this way.

t.zh: 翻拍印刷的照片，或者扫描报纸上的图，常常带上一层规则的网纹：印刷时的网点和相机的像素格子叠在一起，浮出原来没有的条纹。
t.en: Photographing a printed photo, or scanning a picture from a newspaper, often adds a regular screen of stripes: the printing dots and the camera's pixel grid overlap and stripes appear that were never there.

t.zh: 一组规则的条纹，在频谱里是什么样子？照片本身的内容又在频谱的哪里？
t.en: What does a regular set of stripes look like in a spectrum? And where in the spectrum is the photo's own content?

caption.zh: 第一组测试照片的频谱
caption.en: The spectrum of the first test photo

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：按说明里的规则去掉网纹。每张照片的网纹方向和疏密都不一样。
t.en: Your task in this level: remove the screen by the rule in the brief. Each photo's screen has a different direction and spacing.

brief.zh: 翻拍印刷的照片，常常带上一层规则的网纹。在频谱里，网纹是一对很亮的点。去掉频谱里半径 3 以外、比 0.6 还亮的格子，其余保持不变，输出去掉网纹的照片。每张照片的网纹方向和疏密都不一样。
brief.en: A photo of a printed picture often picks up a regular screen pattern. In the spectrum the screen is a pair of very bright dots. Remove the spectrum cells beyond radius 3 that are brighter than 0.6, keep everything else, and output the photo without its screen. Each photo's screen has a different direction and spacing.

hint.zh: 网纹在哪，得从这张照片自己的频谱里找。找到的地方增益为 0，其余为 1。
hint.en: Where the screen is has to be found from this photo's own spectrum. Make the gain 0 where you find it and 1 everywhere else.

after.zh: 这就是朗伯模型：哑光表面的亮度 = 灯 × 反射率 × cos θ。正对着灯最亮，越斜越暗，因为同一束光铺到了更大的面积上；背着灯的地方是 0。
after.en: This is the Lambertian model: the brightness of a matte surface = lamp × reflectance × cos θ. Facing the lamp is brightest, and the more it turns away the darker it gets, because the same beam spreads over a larger area; where the surface faces away it is 0.

t.zh: 正面光下，你已经把表面朝向和反射率结合成亮度。现在灯移到右上方：只看法线的 z 分量不再足够，需要考虑灯与表面的完整方向。
t.en: With frontal light, you combined surface orientation and reflectance into brightness. Now the lamp moves to the upper right: the normal’s z component alone is no longer enough, and the full directions matter.

t.zh: 输入是每一点的单位法线和反射率。灯的方向为 (0.48, −0.36, 0.8)，x 向右、y 向下、z 朝向相机。画出相机拍到的样子。
t.en: The inputs are each point’s unit normal and reflectance. The lamp direction is (0.48, −0.36, 0.8), with x right, y down and z toward the camera. Draw what the camera sees.

brief.zh: 输入是一块表面每一点的朝向（法线的 x、y、z 三个分量）和它的反射率。灯从右上方照来，方向是 (0.48, −0.36, 0.8)（x 向右，y 向下，z 朝着相机）。画出相机拍到的样子：亮度 = 反射率 × cos θ，θ 是法线和灯的方向的夹角。
brief.en: The inputs are which way each point of a surface faces (the x, y and z of its normal) and its reflectance. The lamp shines from the upper right, from direction (0.48, −0.36, 0.8) (x to the right, y down, z towards the camera). Draw what the camera sees: brightness = reflectance × cos θ, where θ is the angle between the normal and the lamp direction.

hint.zh: 两个单位长度的方向，夹角的 cos 等于它们的分量两两相乘再相加。
hint.en: For two directions of unit length, the cos of the angle between them is their components multiplied pairwise and added.

after.zh: 一张照片只给出一个亮度，它同时取决于漆色和朝向，分不开。换一盏灯再拍一张，漆色在两张里一样，比一比就消掉了，剩下的只和朝向有关。这就是光度立体：用几盏已知的灯，从明暗里解出表面的朝向。
after.en: One photo gives one brightness, which depends on both the paint and the facing, and the two cannot be told apart. Take another photo under another lamp: the paint is the same in both, so comparing them cancels it, and what is left depends only on the facing. This is photometric stereo: with a few known lamps, the facing of a surface is solved from its shading.

t.zh: 产线上的金属板刷了漆，要检查有没有磕出的凹坑和划痕。坑和划痕改变的是表面的朝向，可漆色深浅不一，单看一张照片里的明暗，分不清是漆还是坑。这一章最后三关，就来搭这台检测仪。
t.en: Painted metal sheets on a line must be checked for dents and scratches. These change which way the surface faces, but the paint is uneven, so the shading in a single photo cannot tell paint from dent. The last three levels of this chapter build this inspection machine.

t.zh: 每块板在三盏灯下各拍一张：右灯、下灯和正面灯，方向都在说明里。三张照片里，漆色是一样的，变的只是灯。
t.en: Each sheet is photographed under three lamps: from the right, from below and from the front, with their directions in the brief. The paint is the same in all three photos; only the lamp changes.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：一个鼓包，三张照片

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：标出表面朝右倾斜的地方。要想的问题：一张照片里的暗，可能是什么造成的？两张照片之间的什么关系，和漆色无关？
t.en: Your task in this level: mark where the surface leans to the right. Something to think about: what could make a spot dark in one photo? What relation between two photos has nothing to do with the paint?

brief.zh: 产线上的金属板刷了漆，漆色深浅不一。同一块板在三盏灯下各拍一张：灯从右边 (0.6, 0, 0.8)、下边 (0, 0.6, 0.8) 和正面 (0, 0, 1) 照来。标出朝右倾斜的地方：法线的 x 分量超过 z 分量的 0.15 倍。
brief.en: Metal sheets on the line are painted unevenly, some patches darker than others. Each sheet is photographed under three lamps: from the right (0.6, 0, 0.8), from below (0, 0.6, 0.8) and from the front (0, 0, 1). Mark where the surface leans to the right: where the normal's x component is more than 0.15 times its z component.

hint.zh: 一张照片里暗，可能是漆深，也可能是朝向。三张照片里，什么是一样的？
hint.en: Dark in one photo may mean dark paint or a turned-away surface. What is the same in all three photos?

after.zh: 三张照片按固定的系数相减，得到反射率乘上法线的三个分量 ρ·(nx, ny, nz)。法线长度是 1，所以这个向量的长度就是反射率 ρ，方向就是法线。三盏灯，三个方程，三个未知数（加上 ρ 一共四个数，靠「长度为 1」补上最后一个）。
after.en: Subtracting the three photos with fixed weights gives the reflectance times each component of the normal: ρ·(nx, ny, nz). A normal has length 1, so the length of this vector is the reflectance ρ and its direction is the normal. Three lamps, three equations, three unknowns (with ρ there are four numbers, and "length 1" supplies the last one).

t.zh: <level-ref to="3-10"></level-ref>只问了朝右还是朝左。三盏灯其实能告诉你更多：每一点的漆色和朝向，都能解出来。
t.en: <level-ref to="3-10"></level-ref> only asked left or right. Three lamps can tell you more: the paint and the facing at every point can both be solved.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：同样的三张照片，输出漆色本身，也就是每一点的反射率，和表面朝哪边无关。
t.en: Your task in this level: from the same three photos, output the paint itself, the reflectance at every point, whichever way the surface faces.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：鼓包上的漆
caption.en: Set 1: the paint on a bump

brief.zh: 同样的三张照片。这次输出漆色本身：每一点的反射率，和表面朝哪边无关。
brief.en: The same three photos. This time output the paint itself: the reflectance at every point, whichever way the surface faces.

hint.zh: 正面灯的照片是反射率 × nz。另两张各多了一个分量。
hint.en: The front lamp's photo is reflectance × nz. The other two each bring in one more component.

after.zh: 凹坑检测台用的就是光度立体：几盏灯轮流打光，解出每一点的朝向，坑和划痕在朝向图里一目了然，漆色深浅完全不影响。手机拍证件、工厂查钢板表面，都有这样的做法。
after.en: This dent detector is photometric stereo at work: a few lamps light the part in turn, the facing at every point is solved, and dents and scratches stand out in the map of facings, whatever the paint does. Document scanning on phones and steel-sheet inspection in factories use the same approach.

t.zh: 检测仪的最后一关。金属板本该是平的，允许它轻微弯曲；磕出的坑和划痕会让表面明显倾斜。
t.en: The inspection machine's final level. A sheet should be flat, though a slight bend is allowed; dents and scratches make the surface tilt clearly.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：标出坡度超过 0.3 的地方，漆色深浅不能误报。
t.en: Your task in this level: mark where the slope is above 0.3; uneven paint must not raise an alarm.

caption.zh: 第三组测试：一个坑和一道划痕
caption.en: Set 3: a dent and a scratch

brief.zh: 同样的三盏灯。金属板本该是平的（允许轻微弯曲），磕出的凹坑和划痕都会让表面倾斜。标出倾斜得太厉害的地方：表面的坡度（法线水平分量的长度 ÷ nz）超过 0.3。漆色深浅不能误报。
brief.en: The same three lamps. A sheet should be flat (a slight bend is allowed); dents and scratches make the surface tilt. Mark where it tilts too much: where the slope (the length of the normal's horizontal part ÷ nz) is above 0.3. Uneven paint must not raise an alarm.

hint.zh: 上两关各求出了一部分。坡度只和朝向有关。
hint.en: The last two levels each worked out part of it. The slope depends only on the facing.

t.zh: 照片的明暗从哪里来？先从一块白色哑光表面开始：灯从相机方向照来，表面不同位置的倾斜程度会影响收到的光。
t.en: Where does light and shade in a photograph come from? Start with a white matte surface lit from the camera direction. Its orientation affects how much light reaches each point.

t.zh: 表面每一点都有一根垂直于表面的单位法线，表示它的朝向。把这根方向分成三个分量：x 指向右，y 指向下，z 指向相机；正负表示沿轴的哪个方向，大小表示朝那个方向的程度。这三张分量图已经作为输入给出。
t.en: At each point, a unit normal points perpendicular to the surface and describes its orientation. Its three components follow the axes: x points right, y down, and z toward the camera. Their signs give direction along each axis, and their magnitudes show how much of the normal points along it. The three component images are given as inputs.

after.zh: 正面光下，法线的 z 分量给出表面朝向光的程度：正对光的地方最亮，倾斜的地方较暗。
after.en: Under frontal light, the normal’s z component measures how directly the surface faces the light: points facing it are brightest and tilted points are darker.

brief.zh: 灯从正面照来，方向是 (0, 0, 1)。白色表面各点的亮度等于法线与灯方向夹角的余弦。用给出的法线分量画出亮度图；这一关不需要添加任何元件。
brief.en: The light shines from the front, in direction (0, 0, 1). Each point on the white surface has brightness equal to the cosine of the angle between its normal and the light direction. Draw the brightness image from the given normal components; you do not need to add any parts.

hint.zh: 灯的方向只有 z 分量；两个单位方向夹角的余弦，是对应分量相乘后相加。
hint.en: The light direction has only a z component. The cosine between two unit directions is the sum of their pairwise component products.

nx.zh: 法线在左右方向上的分量。鼓包两侧的朝向相反，所以图中一边暗、一边亮。
nx.en: The normal's left–right component. Opposite sides of the bump face opposite ways, so one side of the image is dark and the other light.

ny.zh: 法线在上下方向上的分量。鼓包上下两侧的朝向相反。
ny.en: The normal's up–down component. The upper and lower sides of the bump face opposite ways.

nz.zh: 法线朝向相机的分量。鼓包顶部和平板正对相机，图中较亮；鼓包斜坡较暗。
nz.en: The component of the normal toward the camera. The top of the bump and the flat plate face the camera and appear brighter in this image; the slopes appear darker.

albedo.zh: 表面反射多少光。这里整块表面都是白色，反射率为 1，所以图中全白。
albedo.en: How much light the surface reflects. Here the entire surface is white, with reflectance 1, so the image is white throughout.

t.zh: 正面光下，表面朝向决定光照的强弱；但即使朝向相同，白漆和深色漆也不会一样亮。现在把不同的漆涂到表面上。
t.en: Under frontal light, surface orientation determines illumination; even at the same orientation, white and dark paint do not look equally bright. Now paint the surface with different reflectances.

t.zh: 反射率表示表面反回的光所占比例，输入为每一点的反射率和单位法线。灯仍从相机方向照来。
t.en: Reflectance is the fraction of incident light returned by a surface. The inputs are each point’s reflectance and unit normal; the lamp still shines from the camera direction.

after.zh: 同样的照射下，反射率低的表面返回的光更少；亮度同时取决于照射和反射率。
after.en: Under the same illumination, a lower-reflectance surface returns less light. Brightness depends on both illumination and reflectance.

brief.zh: 灯的方向为 (0, 0, 1)。把表面朝向光的程度与反射率结合，画出不同漆色和不同朝向共同产生的亮度。
brief.en: The light direction is (0, 0, 1). Combine how directly the surface faces the light with its reflectance to draw the brightness produced by both paint and orientation.

hint.zh: 先用法线的 z 分量表示正面光的照射程度，再想想表面只反回其中一部分光。
hint.en: Use the normal’s z component for frontal illumination, then consider that the surface returns only a fraction of that light.

after.zh: 光是相加的：两盏灯照出的亮度，等于各自照出的亮度之和。背对补光的那一面得不到补光，亮度不会变成负数，所以要在 0 截住。摄影棚里的主光加补光、游戏里的多光源，都是这样一盏一盏加起来的。
after.en: Light adds up: the brightness under two lamps is the sum of what each gives on its own. The side facing away from the fill light gets none of it, and brightness cannot be negative, so it is cut off at 0. A key light plus a fill light in a studio, or many lights in a game, are added up lamp by lamp just like this.

t.zh: 摄影棚里很少只用一盏灯：主灯之外，还会在另一侧放一盏弱一些的补光，让暗面不至于漆黑。
t.en: Studios rarely use a single lamp: besides the key light, a weaker fill light goes on the other side so the dark side is not pitch black.

t.zh: <level-ref to="3-1"></level-ref>的电路现在是<part-ref to="lambert"></part-ref>元件：给它法线和反射率，设好灯的方向，它就画出这盏灯下的样子。
t.en: <level-ref to="3-1"></level-ref>'s circuit is now the <part-ref to="lambert"></part-ref> part: give it the normals and the reflectance, set the lamp direction, and it draws the surface under that lamp.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：主灯不变，再加一盏从左边低处照来的补光，强度是主灯的一半。要想的问题：背对补光的那一面，补光给它的亮度是多少？
t.en: Your task in this level: keep the key light and add a fill light low on the left at half its strength. Something to think about: on the side facing away from the fill light, how much brightness does the fill light give?

caption.zh: 第一组测试：一个高鼓包

brief.zh: 主灯不变，再从左边低处加一盏补光，方向 (−0.8, 0, 0.6)，强度是主灯的一半。画出两盏灯一起照的样子。
brief.en: Keep the main lamp and add a fill light low on the left, from direction (−0.8, 0, 0.6), at half the main lamp's strength. Draw what the surface looks like under both lamps.

hint.zh: 两盏灯照亮同一块表面，各自贡献的亮度会怎样合在一起？背对补光的地方呢？
hint.en: Two lamps light the same surface: how do the brightnesses they each give combine? And where the surface faces away from the fill light?

solution: m = shade[lx=0.5, ly=-0.35, lz=0.8](nx, ny, nz, albedo)
f = shade[lx=-0.8, lz=0.6](nx, ny, nz, albedo)
naive: m = shade[lx=0.5, ly=-0.35, lz=0.8](nx, ny, nz, albedo)
alsoFails: m = shade[lx=0.5, ly=-0.35, lz=0.8](nx, ny, nz, albedo)

after.zh: 一整条光谱，被三种感光元件压成三个数，这就是相机（和人眼）看到的颜色。
after.en: A whole spectrum, squeezed by three kinds of sensor into three numbers: that is the colour a camera (and an eye) sees.

t.zh: 彩色照片每个像素有三个数：R、G、B。可现实里的光不止三种，而是像彩虹那样一整条，从紫到红连成一片，叫光谱。
t.en: Each pixel of a colour photo has three numbers: R, G and B. But real light is not three kinds; it is a whole band like a rainbow, from violet to red, called a spectrum.

t.zh: 相机和人眼一样，只有三种感光元件，各自对一段波长敏感。每种元件对每个波长有多敏感，画出来是一条灵敏度曲线。
t.en: A camera, like the human eye, has only three kinds of sensor, each sensitive to a range of wavelengths. How sensitive each is at each wavelength, drawn out, is its sensitivity curve.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：日光的光谱和三条灵敏度曲线
caption.en: Set 1: the daylight spectrum and the three sensitivity curves

t.zh: 这一关的输入都是波形：一条光谱和三条灵敏度曲线，每条 10 个点，从紫到红。<part-ref to="mean"></part-ref>把一行数平均成一个数。
t.en: This level's inputs are all waveforms: a spectrum and three sensitivity curves, 10 points each, from violet to red. <part-ref to="mean"></part-ref> turns a row of numbers into one number.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：算出相机读到的 R、G、B 三个数，分别接到输出的 R、G、B 口，看它们组成的彩色像素。 没接的颜色通道按 0 处理；直接接「图」口则输出整张图。
t.en: Calculate the R, G and B readings and connect them to the matching output ports to see the resulting colour pixel. Unconnected colour channels are zero; connect the Image port to output a whole image directly.

brief.zh: 「光谱」是从紫（400 nm）到红（700 nm）的 10 个波段各有多少光。相机有三种感光元件，各有一条灵敏度曲线。每种的读数 = 光谱乘上它的灵敏度曲线，再求平均。将三个读数接入输出的 R、G、B 口。
brief.en: The "Spectrum" is how much light there is in each of 10 bands from violet (400 nm) to red (700 nm). The camera has three kinds of sensor, each with a sensitivity curve. Each sensor reads the spectrum times its sensitivity curve, averaged. Connect the three readings to the R, G and B output ports.

title.en: A new lamp gives it away

after.zh: 两块布在日光下读数一样，换一盏灯就不一样了：它们的光谱不同，只是差别正好落在三种感光都看不见的地方。这叫同色异谱。买衣服时在店里灯下配好的颜色，到了太阳底下对不上，就是这个原因。感光是线性的，所以「先相减再读数」和「分别读数再相减」一样。
after.en: The two cloths read the same in daylight and differently under another lamp: their spectra differ, but only where none of the three sensors can see. This is metamerism. It is why colours that match under the shop's lights can clash in the sun. Sensing is linear, so "subtract, then read" is the same as "read each, then subtract".

t.zh: 布是什么颜色，要看它把每个波长的光反射回来多少，这也是一条曲线。照到布上的光 × 布的反射，才是进到相机里的光谱。
t.en: What colour a cloth is depends on how much light it reflects at each wavelength, which is another curve. The light falling on the cloth × the cloth's reflectance is the spectrum that enters the camera.

t.zh: <level-ref to="3-3"></level-ref>的电路现在是<part-ref to="sense"></part-ref>元件：选 R、G 或 B，它就按那条灵敏度曲线读一条光谱。
t.en: <level-ref to="3-3"></level-ref>'s circuit is now the <part-ref to="sense"></part-ref> part: choose R, G or B and it reads a spectrum with that sensitivity curve.

t.zh: 这一关有两块布，在日光下相机读到的 R、G、B 一模一样。这一关你要做的：在各种灯下，输出相机读到的布 A 减去布 B。要想的问题：两块布的光谱明明不同，为什么日光下分不出来？
t.en: This level has two cloths whose R, G and B readings are exactly the same in daylight. Your task in this level: under various lamps, output what the camera reads for cloth A minus cloth B. Something to think about: the two cloths' spectra are plainly different, so why can daylight not tell them apart?

caption.zh: 第二组测试：暖白灯下的两块布
caption.en: Set 2: the two cloths under a warm white lamp

brief.zh: 「布 A」「布 B」是两块布在每个波段反射多少光，「灯」是灯的光谱。照到布上再反射进相机的光 = 灯 × 布。输出这盏灯下，相机读到的布 A 减去布 B：R、G、B 三个差。
brief.en: "Cloth A" and "Cloth B" are how much light two cloths reflect in each band, and "Lamp" is the lamp's spectrum. The light that reaches the camera off a cloth = lamp × cloth. Output what the camera reads for cloth A minus cloth B under this lamp: three differences, R, G and B.

hint.zh: 日光那一组的答案全是 0。两块布的光谱明明不一样，相机为什么分不出来？
hint.en: The daylight test expects all zeros. The two cloths' spectra are plainly different, so why can the camera not tell them apart?

after.zh: 照片中的明暗由表面颜色和光照共同决定。在本关的模型里，已知各处光照，就能恢复表面的 RGB 反射率；光完全照不到时，照片不能提供那里的颜色信息。
after.en: Brightness in a photograph depends on both surface colour and illumination. In this model, known illumination lets us recover RGB reflectance; where no light reaches the surface, the photo contains no colour information.

t.zh: 到这里为止，看的都是一块表面。真实照片里，表面本来的颜色和照到的光混在一起：白墙在阴影里是灰的，深色地砖在太阳底下也可能很亮。
t.en: So far you have looked at a single surface. In a real photo, a surface's own colour and the light falling on it are mixed together: a white wall in shadow looks grey, and dark floor tiles in sunlight can look very bright.

t.zh: 找物体，常靠照片里明暗突变的地方。阴影也会造出明暗突变。要想的问题：照片里一条明暗分界线，一定是物体的边吗？手机扫描文件时去掉纸上的阴影，碰到的就是这件事。
t.en: Finding objects often relies on places where brightness jumps. Shadows make brightness jumps too. Something to think about: is a line between light and dark in a photo always the edge of an object? A phone app removing the shadow from a scanned page runs into exactly this.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：两个输入，一张彩色照片和一张光照图（每一点照到多少光，1 是满光）。照片的「图」出口给出整张彩色图，R、G、B 出口分别给出三个通道。输出表面本来的颜色，去掉阴影和明暗。
t.en: Your task: use a colour photo and a lighting map (how much light reaches each point; 1 is full light). The photo’s Image output gives the full colour image; its R, G and B outputs give individual channels. Output the surface’s own colour without shadows or shading.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：照片、光照 → 期望

brief.zh: 照片里每一点的亮度 = 表面本来的颜色（反射率）× 照到那一点的光。第二个输入告诉你每一点照到多少光（1 是满光，阴影里少得多）。去掉阴影和明暗，只输出表面本来的颜色。
brief.en: The brightness of each point in a photo = the surface's own colour (its reflectance) × the light reaching that point. The second input tells you how much light each point gets (1 is full light; in shadow it is much less). Remove the shadows and shading and output only the surface's own colour.

hint.zh: 照片 = 颜色 × 光照。已知其中两个，怎样求第三个？减法行不行，看看阴影里的格子。
hint.en: Photo = colour × lighting. If you know two of them, how do you find the third? To see whether subtracting works, look at the squares in the shadow.

after.zh: 在本关的白光模型里，光照强弱会让 R、G、B 按相同比例变化。辨认颜色时，要看各通道的相对关系，而不是只看某个通道的亮度；这种描述颜色的相对关系称为色度。光源颜色变化或接近全黑时，仅靠这种关系可能无法可靠判断。
after.en: In this level's neutral-light model, changing illumination scales R, G and B together. Identifying colour calls for comparing the channels relative to one another, rather than relying on the brightness of one channel alone. Such a description of colour is called chromaticity. When the light's colour changes or the signal is near black, this relationship alone may not be reliable.

t.zh: 要找红色物体，单看 R 够吗？红苹果在阴影里可能比强光下的浅色苹果有更小的 R。先用两只苹果做实验，再让电路在整个场景里找红色。
t.en: Is R alone enough to find red objects? A red apple in shade can have a smaller R than a pale apple in bright light. First experiment with two apples, then build a circuit to find red throughout a scene.

t.zh: 先比较两只苹果各自的 R、G、B 图。滑动光照强度，观察三张图和数值怎么变化；灯是白光，只改变强弱。再选出红苹果。
t.en: First compare each apple's R, G and B images. Slide the light intensity and watch the three images and values change. The lamp is neutral white; only its strength changes. Then select the red apple.

brief.zh: 两只苹果的颜色不同，在同一盏白灯下。调节光照强度，比较各自的 R、G、B 图与数值，找出红苹果。
brief.en: Two differently coloured apples sit under the same neutral white lamp. Adjust the light intensity, compare their R, G and B images and values, and find the red apple.

hint.zh: 不要只比较两只苹果的 R；分别看看每只苹果的 R 与自己的 G、B 有什么关系，再改变光照试试。
hint.en: Do not compare only the apples' R values. Compare each apple's R with its own G and B, then change the light and try again.

after.zh: 在这个白光模型里，光照把同一个物体的三个通道按相同比例改变，因此可以比较通道之间的比例。接下来把这个想法用于整张图。
after.en: In this neutral-light model, illumination scales all three channels of the same object together, so their proportions can be compared. Next, apply the idea to a whole image.

win.zh: 找到了。比较每只苹果三个通道的相对大小，再试试不同的光强。
win.en: Found it. Compare each apple's three channels with one another, then try different light strengths.

status.zh: 比较各通道后选择苹果，再检查。
status.en: Compare the channels, choose an apple, and check.

brief.zh: 标出场景中所有红色区域，包括亮处和阴影里的红色区域。
brief.en: Mark every red area in the scene, including red areas in both light and shade.

hint.zh: 阴影里的红苹果，R 并不大；阳光下的白纸，R 却很大。光照把三个数一起放大缩小，什么量不受它影响？
hint.en: A red apple in the shade has a small R; white paper in the sun has a big one. Lighting scales all three numbers together, so what stays the same?

after.zh: 两个方向的坡度合成一个长度，边缘强度就和边的方向无关了：横边、竖边、斜边一样亮。方向本身是 atan2(gy, gx)，箭头总指向变亮最快的方向，在边上和边垂直。切到「坡度」画法看输入：箭头就画在每个像素上。
after.en: Combining the slopes in two directions into one length makes edge strength independent of edge direction: horizontal, vertical and diagonal edges are equally bright. The direction itself is atan2(gy, gx); the arrow always points where the brightness rises fastest, and on an edge it is perpendicular to the edge. Draw the input in the "Slope" view: the arrows are drawn at every pixel.

t.zh: 明暗从哪来已经讲完，这一关转向边：明暗变化很快的地方。要找它，先得说清每一点「变得有多快」。
t.en: So much for where light and shade come from. This level turns to edges: places where brightness changes fast. To find them, first say how fast the brightness changes at each point.

t.zh: 坡度有两个分量：往右走亮度变多少（gx），往下走变多少（gy），两个合起来是一个箭头，叫梯度。Sobel x 在每个像素量 gx，Sobel y 量 gy。
t.en: A slope has two components: how much the brightness changes going right (gx), and going down (gy). Together they make an arrow called the gradient. Sobel x measures gx at every pixel, and Sobel y measures gy.

caption.zh: Sobel x 处理圆盘：左右两侧反应强，上下几乎没有
caption.en: Sobel x on a disc: strong on the left and right, almost nothing at the top and bottom

t.zh: 难处在方向。物体的边有横有竖有斜，只量一个方向的坡度会漏掉另一些边。一个好的边缘强度，不该因为边转了个方向就变弱。
t.en: The difficulty is direction. Object edges run horizontally, vertically and diagonally; measuring the slope in one direction only misses some of them. A good edge strength should not get weaker just because an edge turns.

t.zh: 新画法「坡度」：画出等高线，再在各处画一个箭头，指向变亮最快的方向。
t.en: A new way of drawing, "Slope": contour lines, with an arrow at each place pointing where the picture brightens fastest.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：在每个像素输出梯度箭头有多长。测试里有方块、圆盘、字母 X 和一个角，边朝着各个方向。
t.en: Your task in this level: at every pixel, output how long the gradient arrow is. The tests have a square, a disc, a letter X and a corner, with edges facing every way.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：方块 → 期望

brief.zh: 坡度有两个分量：Sobel x 量往右走亮度变多少（gx），Sobel y 量往下走（gy）。两个合成一个箭头，在每个像素输出箭头有多长：√(gx² + gy²)。不管边是横的、竖的还是斜的，越陡的地方越亮。
brief.en: A slope has two components: Sobel x measures how much the brightness changes going right (gx), and Sobel y going down (gy). Together they make an arrow; at every pixel, output how long that arrow is: √(gx² + gy²). Whether an edge is horizontal, vertical or diagonal, the steeper it is, the brighter.

hint.zh: 箭头的长度怎么从两个分量算出来？想想勾股定理。
hint.en: How do you get the arrow's length from its two components? Think of Pythagoras.

after.zh: 求坡度去掉了整体加亮（偏置），除以最陡的坡度去掉了整体倍数（增益）。设计特征时先问：哪些变化不应该改变答案？这叫不变性。注意图外补的数：补 0 会在图边造出一条随灯光变化的假边，所以要复制边缘。
after.en: Taking slopes removes an overall brightening (the offset); dividing by the steepest slope removes an overall scaling (the gain). When you design a feature, first ask: which changes should not change the answer? This is called invariance. Mind the padding outside the image: padding with 0 creates a fake edge at the border that changes with the lighting, so replicate the edge instead.

t.zh: 找边还差一步：定一个门槛，梯度超过它的像素才算边。门槛太低，表面的细纹也算进来；太高，真正的边又会漏掉。
t.en: Finding edges needs one more step: a threshold, so that only pixels whose gradient exceeds it count as edges. Too low, and fine texture counts too; too high, and real edges are missed.

t.zh: 麻烦在灯光。车上的摄像头中午和傍晚都要认出同一条路沿，不可能每换一次光就重调一次门槛。同一张脸在室内和室外，像素数值差得很远，该给的答案却一样。
t.en: The trouble is lighting. A car's camera must recognise the same kerb at noon and at dusk; it cannot retune the threshold every time the light changes. The same face indoors and outdoors gives very different pixel values, yet the answer should be the same.

caption.zh: 同一个 F，灯暗了，期望的边不变
caption.en: The same F with a dimmer lamp: the expected edges stay the same

t.zh: 这一关新出现的元件是<part-ref to="part:globalMax"></part-ref>：找出输入里最大的那个数，输出一张处处都是这个数的图。
t.en: New in this level is the part <part-ref to="part:globalMax"></part-ref>: it finds the largest number in its input and outputs a picture filled with that number everywhere.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：输入是同一个物体在不同灯光下的照片，有的整体变亮，有的变暗。输出它的边，四组测试的期望完全一样。
t.en: Your task in this level: the inputs are photos of the same object under different lighting, some brighter overall, some dimmer. Output its edges; all four tests expect exactly the same answer.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：原来的灯光 → 期望

brief.zh: 同一个物体在不同灯光下拍了几次：有的整体变亮，有的灯暗了一半。每次都要标出同一组边：梯度大小超过这张图里最陡处一半的像素输出 1。
brief.en: The same object was photographed several times under different lighting: in some shots it is brighter overall, in others the light is half as strong. Each time, mark the same set of edges: output 1 at pixels whose gradient magnitude is more than half that of the steepest spot in the picture.

hint.zh: 不知道灯暗了多少，能不能在图里找一把跟着灯光一起变长变短的尺子？
hint.en: You don't know how much the light dimmed. Can you find a ruler inside the image that grows and shrinks with the light?

after.zh: 白平衡利用场景中对颜色的假设，估计并校正光源带来的偏色。本关假设白纸在三个通道中各自最亮；如果画面没有白色物体，或者光源、表面的情况更复杂，这种假设可能不成立。
after.en: White balance uses assumptions about scene colours to estimate and correct a light source’s colour cast. Here the white paper is assumed brightest in each channel; this can fail without a white object or under more complicated lighting and surfaces.

t.zh: 这是一道挑战关，可以跳过。它不需要新元件。
t.en: This is a challenge level, and you can skip it. It needs no new parts.

t.zh: 在偏黄的灯下拍照，白纸会发黄，整张照片都带着灯的颜色。人眼会自动纠正，相机得靠「白平衡」。
t.en: Photographed under a yellowish lamp, white paper looks yellow and the whole picture takes on the lamp's colour. Your eyes correct for it automatically; a camera needs "white balance".

caption.zh: 第一组测试：黄灯下的书桌
caption.en: Set 1: a desk under a yellow lamp

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：每张彩色照片里都有白纸，它在 R、G、B 通道中都是最亮的。从照片的 R、G、B 出口分别取出通道，调整后接入输出的对应接口，让白纸变回纯白。
t.en: Each colour photo contains white paper, brightest in each R, G and B channel. Take the channels from the photo’s R, G and B outputs, adjust them, and connect them to the matching output ports to make the paper white.

brief.zh: 这些照片是在偏黄的灯下拍的，白纸看上去发黄。每张照片里都有一块白纸，而且它在 R、G、B 里都是最亮的。把三个通道各自调整，让白纸变成纯白 (1, 1, 1)，其余颜色跟着一起还原。
brief.en: These photos were taken under a yellowish lamp, so white paper looks yellow. Every photo has a patch of white paper in it, the brightest thing in each of R, G and B. Adjust each channel so the paper becomes pure white (1, 1, 1), and every other colour is restored along with it.

hint.zh: 白纸本来应该是什么颜色？
hint.en: What colour should the white paper really be?

after.zh: 训练就是下山：把误差（差的平方的平均）看成地形，w 是你站的位置。每一步沿坡往下挪「学习率 × 坡度」。学习率太小，要走很多步；太大，会冲过谷底，越冲越远。一个网络有上百万个旋钮，原理完全一样。
after.en: Training is walking downhill: think of the error (the mean of the squared differences) as a landscape, with w as where you stand. Each step moves down the slope by "learning rate × slope". Too small a learning rate takes many steps; too large overshoots the bottom and flies further away each time. A network has millions of knobs, and the principle is exactly the same.

t.zh: 前几章，元件的参数都是你亲手定的：模糊多少、阈值多高。可手机相册认人脸、语音输入听写，背后的模型有成千上万个数，没人能一个个拧。机器得自己调。
t.en: In earlier chapters you set every part's parameters by hand: how much blur, how high a threshold. But the models behind face recognition in your photo app or voice typing have thousands upon thousands of numbers, and nobody can turn them one by one. The machine has to tune itself.

t.zh: 要自己调，先得知道「现在调得有多差」。这个分数叫误差：模型的输出离样本的正确答案有多远，平方后取平均。误差越小越好。
t.en: To tune itself, it first needs to know how badly tuned it is right now. That score is the error: how far the model's outputs are from the samples' correct answers, squared and averaged. The smaller the error, the better.

t.zh: 新元件<part-ref to="part:lrnConst"></part-ref>是一个数，这个数不用你填，把它和输入相乘就是 w × 输入。电路里有可学习的元件时，面板里会出现<wiki-ref to="training"></wiki-ref>：每按一步，机器摸一摸误差往哪边下坡，就把旋钮往那边挪一点。
t.en: The new part <part-ref to="part:lrnConst"></part-ref> is a number you do not fill in; multiply the input by it and you have w × input. When a circuit has learnable parts, <wiki-ref to="training"></wiki-ref> appears in the panel: at every step the machine feels which way the error slopes down and nudges the knob that way.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：每组测试是一个样本，让机器自己找出那个数。要想的问题：每一步该迈多大？迈得太小、太大，各会怎样？
t.en: Your task in this level: each test is one sample; let the machine find the number itself. Something to think about: how big should each step be? What happens if the steps are too small, or too big?

brief.zh: 每组测试是一个样本：输入一个亮度，期望一个亮度，规律是 输出 = w × 输入，w 不知道。用<part-ref to="part:lrnConst"></part-ref>当 w，按训练让机器自己找它。选一个学习率。
brief.en: Each test is one sample: a brightness in, a brightness expected out, following output = w × input with w unknown. Use a <part-ref to="part:lrnConst"></part-ref> as w and press Train to let the machine find it. Choose a learning rate.

hint.zh: 学习率是每一步迈多大。太小要走很多步；太大会怎样？看误差曲线。
hint.en: The learning rate is how big each step is. Too small takes many steps; what happens if it is too big? Watch the error curve.

after.zh: 每层只看 3×3，可第二层看的是第一层的输出，等于看到了 5×5；第三层看到 7×7。这叫感受野：叠 L 层 3×3，感受野是 (2L+1)×(2L+1)。VGG 就靠堆小核看大范围，而且三层 3×3 只有 27 个权重，一个 7×7 核要 49 个。
after.en: Each layer looks at only 3×3, but the second layer looks at the first layer's output, so in effect it sees 5×5; the third sees 7×7. This is the receptive field: stack L layers of 3×3 and the receptive field is (2L+1)×(2L+1). VGG sees large areas by stacking small kernels, and three 3×3 layers have only 27 weights, while a single 7×7 kernel needs 49.

t.zh: 3×3 的元件只看得见自己和身边一圈，一共 9 格。可一张脸、一个车轮，在图上远比 3×3 大。网络怎样认出大的东西？
t.en: A 3×3 part only sees its own pixel and the ring around it, 9 cells in all. But a face or a wheel is far bigger than 3×3 in an image. How does a network recognise big things?

t.zh: 这一关要判断：一个格子周围 7×7 的范围是不是全亮。测试里特意放了小一些的方块、长条，还有缺了一个角的 7×7。
t.en: This level asks: is the 7×7 area around a cell entirely bright? The tests deliberately include smaller squares, long bars, and a 7×7 square with one corner missing.

caption.zh: 另一组：一个 5×5、一个 3×3 的方块
caption.en: Another set: a 5×5 square and a 3×3 square

t.zh: 有时同一张图里既有小物体，也有大物体。除了叠起来看得更远，还可以让几条路同时看不同大小的范围，再把结果合在一起。Inception 网络就用这样的多尺度分支。
t.en: A single image can contain both small and large objects. Besides stacking layers to see farther, several paths can look at different-sized regions at the same time and combine their results. Inception networks use such multi-scale branches.

t.zh: 模型可以加深、增加通道，或者看更高分辨率的图；这些选择都可能增加计算量，效果也要用新样本检查。EfficientNet 研究如何在计算预算下共同调整深度、宽度和分辨率。
t.en: A model can be made deeper, given more channels, or shown higher-resolution images. Each choice can increase computation, and its benefit must be checked on new samples. EfficientNet studies how to adjust depth, width and resolution together within a computing budget.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：手里只有看 3×3 的元件，做出看 7×7 的判断。要想的问题：「7×7」能从哪里来？
t.en: Your task: using only parts that look at 3×3, make a judgement about 7×7. Something to think about: where can "7×7" come from?

brief.zh: 只在“周围 7×7 全是亮的”格子输出 1，其余输出 0。手里只有 3×3 的元件。
brief.en: Output 1 only at pixels where "the whole 7×7 around it is bright", and 0 everywhere else. You only have 3×3 parts.

hint.zh: 一个 3×3 只看得到身边一圈。如果第二层看的是第一层的结果，它其实看到了多大？
hint.en: A 3×3 sees only the ring of pixels right around it. If a second layer looks at the first layer's result, how much does it really see?

label.en: 9×9 missing a pixel on one edge

after.zh: 先让每格和右边、下边的邻居比一比，留下最大的，再隔点取样：每个 2×2 块只留下块里最强的那个数，点在块内挪动，答案不变。这就是最大池化。代价是丢掉了块内的精确位置。
after.en: First let each pixel compare itself with its neighbours to the right and below and keep the largest, then downsample: each 2×2 block keeps only its strongest value, and a point moving within its block does not change the answer. This is max pooling. The price is losing the exact position inside the block.

t.zh: 同一个东西拍两次，总会差一点：手一抖，它就往旁边偏了一两个像素。可它还是那个东西，识别的结果不该跟着变。
t.en: Photograph the same thing twice and the shots always differ a little: your hand shakes and it moves a pixel or two to the side. But it is still the same thing, and what it is recognised as should not change.

t.zh: 网络还要不断把图缩小。这一关的输入是几个亮的特征点，要把 16×16 缩成 8×8。
t.en: A network also keeps shrinking the image. The input in this level is a few bright feature points, and you have to shrink 16×16 down to 8×8.

caption.en: Set 1: the feature points in their original place

t.zh: 有时特征点会整体偏一格。这一关的要求是：偏了一格，缩小后的结果也要和原位时完全一样。
t.en: Sometimes all the feature points are off by one pixel. This level's requirement: off by one pixel, the shrunk result must be exactly the same as in place.

caption.zh: 另一组：整体偏到右下，期望不变
caption.en: Another set: everything shifted down and to the right, same expected output

brief.zh: 同一组特征点有时会偏一格。把 16×16 缩成 8×8，偏一格时结果必须完全一样。
brief.en: The same set of keypoints is sometimes off by one pixel. Shrink 16×16 to 8×8; when they shift by one pixel, the result must be exactly the same.

hint.zh: 隔点取样会因为偏一格而错过亮点。能不能在扔掉点之前，让每个点先「知道」它旁边有没有亮点？
hint.en: Downsampling misses bright points when they shift by one pixel. Before throwing pixels away, can each one first "know" whether there is a bright point beside it?

after.zh: 这是一个最小的卷积网络：卷积找局部笔画，ReLU 把“有”和“没有”分开，池化和全局平均让答案不管字母在哪，全连接加 Sigmoid 把特征变成分数。要是一路全是线性运算（没有 ReLU，也没有最大池化），最后只剩“整张图有多亮”，而淡的 X 和浓的 O 一样亮。
after.en: This is the smallest convolutional network: the convolution finds local strokes, ReLU separates "there" from "not there", pooling and global average make the answer the same wherever the letter is, and the dense layer plus sigmoid turns features into a score. If every operation along the way were linear (no ReLU and no max pooling), all that would be left is "how bright the whole image is", and a faint X is as bright as a strong O.

t.zh: 手写数字识别、拍照认花、相册按人脸分组，问的都是「这是什么」。这类问题叫分类，是视觉里最常见的任务。这一关做最小的一个：只有两类，X 或 O。
t.en: Reading handwritten digits, identifying a flower from a photo, grouping an album by face: they all ask "what is this?". This kind of problem is called classification, the most common task in vision. This level does the smallest one: just two classes, X or O.

t.zh: <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>里的神经元拿到的是现成的两个数：斜笔画多少、弯笔画多少。这一关没人替你算，网络只拿到像素，字母还会挪位置、变深浅、带噪点。
t.en: The neuron in <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref> was handed two ready-made numbers: how many diagonal strokes, how many curved strokes. This time nobody computes them for you. The network gets only pixels, and the letters move around, get lighter or darker, and carry noise.

caption.zh: 一组测试：挪了位置、带噪点的 O
caption.en: One test set: an O that has moved and has noise

t.zh: 手里的元件：<part-ref to="part:lrnConv"></part-ref>是从很小的随机数开始的可学习 3×3 核；<part-ref to="mean"></part-ref>把整张图变成一个数；「全连接」和<part-ref to="sigmoid"></part-ref>是你在前面搭出来的。
t.en: The parts to hand: <part-ref to="part:lrnConv"></part-ref> is a learnable 3×3 kernel that starts from very small random numbers; <part-ref to="mean"></part-ref> turns a whole picture into one number; "Dense" and <part-ref to="sigmoid"></part-ref> are what you built earlier.

t.zh: 训练分类器时，也可以把训练图做适合任务的变化，例如轻微平移、改变亮度，再让模型学习它们仍属于同一类。这叫数据增强；变化不能把类别或答案改变。
t.en: When training a classifier, we can also make task-appropriate changes to training images, such as small shifts or brightness changes, and teach the model that they still belong to the same class. This is data augmentation; the changes must preserve the correct label.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：输出一个数，X 大于 0.6，O 小于 0.4。要想的问题：X 和 O 到底差在哪里，什么信息该留下？
t.en: Your task: output one number, above 0.6 for X and below 0.4 for O. Something to think about: what really is the difference between X and O, and which information should be kept?

brief.zh: 输出一个数：是 X 就大于 0.6，是 O 就小于 0.4。字母会挪位置、变深浅、带噪点。
brief.en: Output one number: above 0.6 for an X, below 0.4 for an O. The letters move around, vary in strength and carry noise.

hint.zh: 最后的全连接加 Sigmoid 就是<level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>里那个神经元，把特征变成分数。字母会挪位置、会变深浅，前面要怎样把图变成这样的特征？搭好后按训练。
hint.en: The final dense layer plus sigmoid is the neuron from <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>, turning features into a score. The letters move around and vary in strength: how should the parts before it turn the image into such features? Once it is built, press Train.

after.zh: 多通道卷积同时利用各通道及其邻域的信息。颜色发生变化而整体明暗不变时，合并成一张灰度图可能丢掉区别；保留通道之间的关系，就能识别这样的颜色边界。
after.en: Multichannel convolution uses each channel and its neighbourhood together. A colour boundary can disappear when channels are combined into one greyscale image; keeping their relationships makes such boundaries detectable.

t.zh: 第三章里，彩色照片的每个像素都有 R、G、B 三个数。这一关要把它们作为三个通道一起处理：照片的 R、G、B 出口分别给出各自的数值图。
t.en: In chapter 3, each pixel of a colour photo had R, G and B values. Here you will process them as three channels: the photo’s R, G and B outputs provide the individual value maps.

t.zh: 有些边只有颜色在变，亮度不变，比如一样亮的红和绿挨在一起。色盲检测图就是这样画的：只看明暗的眼睛，看不出里面的数字。
t.en: Some edges change only in colour, not in brightness, such as equally bright red and green side by side. Colour-blindness test plates are drawn this way: an eye that only sees light and dark cannot make out the number inside.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：只描出红和绿的交界，单纯变亮变暗、或只有蓝色在变的地方都要是 0。要想的问题：三张图各自看得到什么，看不到什么？
t.en: Your task: trace only the boundary between red and green. Places that just get brighter or darker, or where only blue changes, must be 0. Something to think about: what can each of the three images see, and what can it not?

caption.zh: 第一组：红绿对半，一样亮
caption.en: Set 1: half red, half green, equally bright

brief.zh: 输入是一张彩色照片，可以从 R、G、B 出口分别取出三个通道。只描出红与绿交界处的边，只是变亮变暗、或只有蓝色在变的地方输出 0。
brief.en: The input is a colour photo; its R, G and B outputs provide the three channels. Trace only the edges where red meets green; output 0 where things only get brighter or darker, or where only blue changes.

hint.zh: 加成灰度图试试：红和绿一样亮时，交界就消失了。那三个通道该怎样处理，才不会丢掉这条边？ 训练时可以先给每个通道减去 0.5，让数据围绕 0 分布。
hint.en: Try adding them into a greyscale image: when red and green are equally bright, the border disappears. So how should the three channels be handled so this edge is not lost? For training, you can first subtract 0.5 from each channel to centre the data around zero.

label.en: Half red, half green, equally bright
Red spot on green, with a blue patch beside it
Red and green split diagonally, darker at the top
Blue bar on a grey gradient

after.zh: 颜色可以通过各通道之间的关系区分：即使整体明暗接近，蓝和黄也能呈现不同的通道组合。不同的滤波器可以关注不同的颜色对比。
after.en: Colours can be distinguished by the relationships among channels: blue and yellow have different channel combinations even at similar overall brightness. Different filters can focus on different colour contrasts.

t.zh: <level-ref to="4-13"></level-ref>的核分辨的是红和绿。颜色还有另一组对立：蓝和黄。沙漠的天际线、海边的沙滩，交界两边常常一样亮，只是颜色不同。
t.en: The kernel in <level-ref to="4-13"></level-ref> told red from green. Colour has another opposition: blue and yellow. On a desert skyline or a beach, the two sides of the border are often equally bright and differ only in colour.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="lrn-rgb"></part-ref>一个核横跨 R、G、B 三张图，27 个权重一起训练。
t.en: The <part-ref to="lrn-rgb"></part-ref> in the tray spans the R, G and B images with one kernel, its 27 weights trained together.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：只描出蓝与黄的交界，只是变亮变暗的地方要是 0。要想的问题：黄色和蓝色，在三张图里各是什么样？
t.en: Your task: trace only the border between blue and yellow; places that just get brighter or darker must be 0. Something to think about: what do yellow and blue each look like in the three images?

caption.zh: 第一组：天和沙，一条平线
caption.en: Set 1: sky and sand, a level line

brief.zh: 输入是一张彩色风景，从 R、G、B 出口可以分别读取三个通道。只描出蓝与黄交界处的边，只是变亮变暗的地方输出 0。
brief.en: The input is a colour landscape; its R, G and B outputs provide the separate channels. Trace only the edges where blue meets yellow; output 0 where things only get brighter or darker.

hint.zh: 黄色的光，是哪两种颜色的光加起来的？ 训练时可以先给每个通道减去 0.5，让数据围绕 0 分布。
hint.en: Yellow light is made of which two colours of light added together? For training, you can first subtract 0.5 from each channel to centre the data around zero.

label.en: Sky and sand, a level line

after.zh: 红灯既要足够亮，也要呈现红色；只看一个通道容易把白色路灯或暗处的红车混进来。结合通道信息，才能在本关的场景里区分这些情况。
after.en: A red light must be both bright enough and red. A single channel can confuse it with white street lamps or dark red cars; combining channel information distinguishes them in these scenes.

t.zh: 在<level-ref to="4-13"></level-ref>里，一个核横跨三个通道，学会了看颜色的对比。这一关在街景里找红灯：红灯又亮又红，可街上还有暗处的红车、白色的路灯和绿灯。
t.en: In <level-ref to="4-13"></level-ref> one kernel spanned three channels and learned to see colour contrast. This level looks for red lights in street scenes: a red light is bright and red, but the street also has red cars in the shade, white street lamps and green lights.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：只标出红灯。要想的问题：「亮」和「红」，各要看哪几个通道？
t.en: Your task in this level: mark only the red lights. Something to think about: which channels does "bright" need, and which does "red"?

brief.zh: 输入是一张彩色街景，可以从 R、G、B 出口分别读取通道。只标出红灯：又亮又红的地方。暗处的红车、白色的路灯、绿灯都不算。
brief.en: The input is a colour street scene; its R, G and B outputs provide the channels. Mark only the red lights: places both bright and red. Red cars in the shade, white street lamps and green lights do not count.

hint.zh: 一个通道只能回答一个问题。「红」和「亮」各要看哪些通道？
hint.en: One channel can only answer one question. Which channels does "red" need, and which does "bright"?

title.en: The deep net that will not train

after.zh: 残差连接让输入沿捷径通过，并让卷积分支学习调整量：y = x + F(x)。当目标接近输入时，网络可以从接近原样通过的状态开始，再学习需要的改变。捷径也为梯度提供直接路径，但并不保证所有深层网络都能训练成功。这里的锐化任务本身很简单，不要求每一层都学到不同特征。
after.en: A residual connection passes the input along a shortcut and lets the convolution branch learn an adjustment: y = x + F(x). When the target is close to the input, the network can start near the identity and learn the needed change. The shortcut also provides a direct path for gradients, but does not guarantee that every deep network will train successfully. The sharpening task here is simple and does not require every layer to learn a different feature.

t.zh: 网络堆得更深，可以让后面的层组合前面的结果，看到更大范围的特征。但层数一多，训练也可能变得困难。
t.en: A deeper network can combine earlier results in later layers to see features over a wider area. But as layers accumulate, training can also become difficult.

t.zh: 先训练两层卷积，观察每一层如何扩大看到的范围。接着尝试训练六层网络，看看怎样让信号通过深层网络。
t.en: First train two convolution layers and observe how each expands the area seen. Then try training a six-layer network and see how to help signals travel through it.

brief.zh: 训练两层 3×3 卷积，让输出呈现较大范围的亮度分布。目标等于连续做两次 3×3 平均；先观察亮点测试中，每一层的结果覆盖了多大范围。
brief.en: Train two 3×3 convolution layers to show brightness over a wider area. The target is two successive 3×3 averages; first observe how wide an area each layer covers in the bright-dot test.

hint.zh: 把两个卷积层串起来，训练它们；比较亮点经过第一层和第二层的图。一个 3×3 层能看到多远，两层又能看到多远？
hint.en: Connect two convolution layers in sequence and train them. Compare the bright dot after the first and second layers: how far can one 3×3 layer see, and how far can two?

after.zh: 第一层从附近提取亮度，第二层再组合第一层的结果，因而能看见更大的范围。这里学到的是简单的亮度分布特征；真实网络还可以逐层组合边缘、形状等更复杂的特征。
after.en: The first layer extracts nearby brightness, and the second combines those results to see a wider area. Here the learned feature is a simple brightness distribution; real networks can also combine edges, shapes and other more complex features across layers.

brief.zh: 把至少 6 个卷积层串成一条路，训练它做一次轻微的锐化：输出 = 原图 + 0.25 ×（原图 − 3×3 平均）。
brief.en: Chain at least 6 conv layers into one path and train it to do a light sharpen: output = image + 0.25 × (image − 3×3 average).

hint.zh: 每层都从很小的随机数开始，图每过一层就缩小几十倍。有没有办法让一层的权重哪怕很小，图也不至于缩没？
hint.en: Every layer starts from very small random numbers, so the image shrinks tens of times over at each layer. Is there a way for a layer to keep the image from shrinking away even when its weights are tiny?

after.zh: 十二层和六层一样好训：每一块一开始都原样通过，训练只需让少数几块学出那一点改动，梯度沿着捷径直达每一层。ResNet 就这样把网络堆到了一百多层。
after.en: Twelve layers train as easily as six: every block starts out passing its input straight through, training only has to teach a few of them the small change, and the gradient reaches every layer along the shortcuts. This is how ResNet stacks networks to more than a hundred layers.

t.zh: <level-ref to="4-16"></level-ref>里，6 层的网络加上捷径就训得动了。今天认图的网络动辄上百层，再深下去还行吗？
t.en: In <level-ref to="4-16"></level-ref>, a 6-layer network trained once it had shortcuts. Today's image-recognition networks run to a hundred layers or more: does it still work deeper down?

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：把至少 12 个卷积层串成一条路，训练它学会测试里那种轻微的模糊。每个卷积层都从很小的随机数开始。
t.en: Your task: chain at least 12 conv layers into one path and train it to learn the light blur in the tests. Every conv layer starts from very small random numbers.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：字母 X → 轻微模糊
caption.en: Set 1: the letter X → lightly blurred

brief.zh: 把至少 12 个卷积层串成一条路，训练它做测试里那种轻微的模糊。
brief.en: Chain at least 12 conv layers into one path and train it to do the light blur in the tests.

hint.zh: <level-ref to="4-16"></level-ref>里每一层是怎样接的？托盘里的<part-ref to="lrn-res"></part-ref>一个元件就是那样一块。
hint.en: How was each layer wired in <level-ref to="4-16"></level-ref>? A <part-ref to="lrn-res"></part-ref> part in the tray is one such block.

after.zh: 深度可分离卷积把空间处理和通道混合分开。它可以减少计算，但一个输入通道对应的空间核要供各输出共享；普通卷积可以为不同输出选择不同的空间核。在这个单输入、一个空间核的例子中，两个独立方向无法同时由同一个核产生。增加中间通道可以改变这种限制，也会增加计算。
after.en: Depthwise separable convolution separates spatial processing from channel mixing. It can reduce computation, but the spatial kernel for an input channel is shared across outputs; ordinary convolution can choose different spatial kernels for each output. In this one-input, one-spatial-kernel example, two independent directions cannot both come from the same kernel. More intermediate channels can change this limit, at additional cost.

t.zh: 手机需要省计算，但省下的计算会不会带来代价？这次比较两种卷积结构，看看它们能做出什么样的空间特征。
t.en: Phones need to save computation, but does saving computation have a cost? Compare two convolution structures and see which spatial features they can produce.

t.zh: 实验简化为一个输入通道、两个输出通道。图中每个 3×3 方格表示输入通道对一个输出的空间核，亮格的权重为 1，暗格为 0，灰格为 0.5。
t.en: This experiment uses one input channel and two output channels. Each 3×3 grid is the spatial kernel from the input to one output: white has weight 1, black 0 and grey 0.5.

t.zh: 普通卷积给两个输出各用一个空间核；深度可分离卷积先用一个空间核处理输入，再送到两个输出。这里两个逐点混合权重固定为 1；空间核可以选择。
t.en: Ordinary convolution uses a separate spatial kernel for each output. Depthwise separable convolution first applies one spatial kernel to the input, then sends the result to both outputs. Here the two pointwise mixing weights are fixed at 1; you can choose the spatial kernels.

t.zh: 台上的计算量只数每个位置的乘法：普通卷积两个 3×3 核需要 18 次；分离结构一个 3×3 核加两个逐点乘法需要 11 次。真实网络还有加法等开销。
t.en: The bench counts only multiplications per position: two ordinary 3×3 kernels need 18; one spatial kernel plus two pointwise multiplications needs 11. Real networks also have additions and other costs.

brief.zh: 比较两种卷积结构：先在计算预算内做出相同的两个空间核，再尝试做出不同的两个核。
brief.en: Compare two convolution structures: first make two identical spatial kernels within a computation budget, then try to make two different kernels.

hint.zh: 深度可分离结构中，两个输出共享空间核 1；普通卷积的两个空间核可以分别选择。
hint.en: In the separable structure both outputs share spatial kernel 1; ordinary convolution can choose its two spatial kernels independently.

note.zh: 两张目标都需要横向的空间核。调整结构和核，让结果符合目标，乘法次数不超过 11。
note.en: Both targets need a horizontal spatial kernel. Adjust the structure and kernels to match them using at most 11 multiplications.

win.zh: 共享空间核可以满足两个相同的目标，再分别送到两个输出。
win.en: A shared spatial kernel meets both identical targets, then feeds both outputs.

note.zh: 现在第一张目标要横向核，第二张要纵向核。先试试深度可分离结构：调整空间核 1 时，两张结果怎样变化？再选出能同时满足目标的结构。
note.en: Now the first target needs a horizontal kernel and the second a vertical one. Try the separable structure first: what happens to both results when you change spatial kernel 1? Then choose a structure that meets both targets.

win.zh: 这个例子中，一个共享空间核不能同时变成横向和纵向；普通卷积可以分别选择两个核。
win.en: In this example one shared spatial kernel cannot be both horizontal and vertical; ordinary convolution can choose two kernels independently.

after.zh: 训练误差一直降，新样本（验证集）的误差却先降后升：后半段模型在背噪声，这叫过拟合。办法一是提前停止，在验证误差最低时停下；办法二是正则化，给大权重加代价（L2），让模型不愿意为了几个点把曲线拧得很弯。λ 太小拦不住过拟合，太大又让模型连真规律都学不会（欠拟合）。真正训练网络时，留一部分数据只用来验证，就是为了看到这条先降后升的线。
after.en: The training error keeps falling, but the error on new samples (the validation set) falls and then rises: in the second half the model is memorising noise. This is called overfitting. One fix is early stopping: stop where the validation error is lowest. The other is regularisation: put a cost on large weights (L2), so the model will not bend the curve sharply just to hit a few points. Too small a λ cannot hold off overfitting; too large and the model cannot learn even the true rule (underfitting). When training real networks, part of the data is kept back for validation only, precisely so you can see this falls-then-rises line.

t.zh: 考试前把往年题连答案一起背下来，旧题全对，新题照样不会。模型也会这样：它在训练样本上越来越准，不等于它在新样本上也准。
t.en: Memorise past exam papers with their answers before a test and you get every old question right, but still cannot do the new ones. Models do this too: getting more and more accurate on the training samples does not mean being accurate on new samples.

t.zh: 所以要留一些模型从没见过的样本，专门拿来检查。台上的实心点是训练样本，空心点是新样本；样本都带一点随机的偏差（噪声），真实规律是一条平滑的曲线。
t.en: So you keep back some samples the model has never seen, just for checking. On the bench the filled dots are training samples and the hollow dots are new samples. Every sample carries a little random deviation (noise); the true pattern is a smooth curve.

t.zh: 这里用新样本选择停止时机和正则化强度，所以它们相当于验证集。真实项目还要留一份测试集，等选择完成后再评估；反复看测试集来调模型，会让最终成绩不再可靠。
t.en: Here the new samples help choose when to stop and how much to regularise, so they act as a validation set. Real projects also keep a test set for evaluation after those choices are made. Repeatedly tuning against the test set makes the final score unreliable.

t.zh: 还有一种正则化叫 Dropout：训练时随机暂时关掉一些神经元，让网络不要过度依赖某条固定路径；验证和测试时不再随机关掉。这个机关台演示的是提前停止和 L2，不模拟 Dropout。
t.en: Another kind of regularisation is dropout: during training, randomly switch off some neurons temporarily so the network does not rely too heavily on a fixed path. Validation and testing do not randomly switch them off. This bench demonstrates early stopping and L2, not dropout.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：决定训练到哪一步该停，再试另一种管住模型的办法。要想的问题：训练误差越来越小时，模型在新样本上是不是也越来越好？
t.en: Your task: decide at which step training should stop, then try another way of keeping the model in check. Something to think about: as the training error keeps shrinking, does the model keep getting better on new samples too?

brief.zh: 训练越久，模型在训练样本上越准。可我们要的是它在没见过的新样本上也准。一个灵活的模型训练太久，会把样本里的噪声也背下来。
brief.en: The longer you train, the more accurate the model gets on the training samples. But what we want is for it to be accurate on new samples it has never seen as well. A flexible model trained too long memorises the noise in the samples too.

hint.zh: 盯住两条误差线：训练误差一直往下走，新样本的误差先下降、后上升。上升的时候，模型在学什么？
hint.en: Keep your eye on the two error lines: the training error keeps going down, while the error on new samples first falls, then rises. While it rises, what is the model learning?

note.zh: 实心点是训练用的 10 个样本（带噪声），空心点是没给模型看过的新样本。拖动「训练了多少步」，看曲线怎样变，下面两条误差线怎样走。停在新样本误差最低的那一步。
note.en: The filled dots are the 10 training samples (with noise); the hollow dots are new samples the model has never been shown. Drag "Steps trained" and watch how the curve changes and how the two error lines below move. Stop at the step where the error on new samples is lowest.

note.zh: 这次一直训练到底，但误差里多加一项：权重越大越受罚（λ × 所有权重的平方和）。调 λ，让新样本的误差尽量低。
note.en: This time training runs to the end, but the error gets an extra term: the larger the weights, the bigger the penalty (λ × the sum of all the squared weights). Tune λ to make the error on new samples as low as you can.

win.zh: 新样本误差已接近最低。
win.en: The error on new samples is close to its minimum.

status.en: The error on new samples is still too high.

after.zh: 两个旋钮时，误差是一片地形，梯度是一个箭头，指向上坡最陡的方向。这片山谷又窄又长，梯度总指着谷壁，路线就走成了之字形。w × 输入 + b 有一个名字：全连接层（这里只有一个输入）。
after.en: With two knobs the error is a landscape, and the gradient is an arrow pointing up the steepest slope. This valley is long and narrow, so the gradient keeps pointing at the valley walls and the path zig-zags. w × input + b has a name: a dense layer (here with a single input).

t.zh: <level-ref to="4-1"></level-ref>只有一个旋钮。这一关的规律多了一项：输出 = w × 输入 + b，两个旋钮要一起调。
t.en: <level-ref to="4-1"></level-ref> had a single knob. This level's rule has one more term: output = w × input + b, and the two knobs must be tuned together.

t.zh: w 和 b 各用一个<part-ref to="part:lrnConst"></part-ref>。
t.en: Use one <part-ref to="part:lrnConst"></part-ref> for w and another for b.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：让机器自己找到 w 和 b。要想的问题：两个旋钮时，「往下坡走」指的是往哪个方向走？
t.en: Your task in this level: let the machine find w and b itself. Something to think about: with two knobs, which direction does "walking downhill" mean?

brief.zh: 规律变成 输出 = w × 输入 + b。两个旋钮都要机器自己找。
brief.en: The rule becomes output = w × input + b. The machine has to find both knobs itself.

hint.zh: 两个旋钮一起下山。山谷又窄又长时，学习率大了会在两侧来回冲，小了又走得很慢。
hint.en: Both knobs walk downhill together. When the valley is long and narrow, a large learning rate bounces from side to side, and a small one crawls.

after.zh: 这叫 Softmax：先用 e 的几次方把分变成正数，再除以总和。分差 1，概率就差 e 倍，最高分会被放大。分类网络的最后一步几乎都是它。
after.en: This is the softmax: first make the scores positive with e to the power of each, then divide by the total. A difference of 1 in score is a factor of e in probability, so the top score is magnified. Almost every classification network ends with it.

t.zh: 分拣机要辨认 X、O、+ 三种零件。相机拍一张，网络先给每一类打一个分，再判断它是哪一种。
t.en: The sorting machine needs to recognise X, O and + parts. From a camera image, the network first gives each class a score and then decides which kind it is.

t.zh: 三选一时，网络先给每一类打一个分。可分数可正可负，加起来也不是 1，不能直接当成「有多大把握」。
t.en: Choosing one of three, the network first gives each class a score. But scores can be positive or negative and do not add up to 1, so they cannot be read as "how sure" directly.

t.zh: 训练分类器还需要衡量预测有多错。常用的交叉熵关注正确类别的概率：给正确类别的概率越低，损失越大。游戏里的训练器使用平方误差，这是另一种损失。
t.en: Training a classifier also needs a measure of how wrong a prediction is. Cross-entropy, a common choice, looks at the probability assigned to the correct class: the lower that probability, the larger the loss. The game trainer uses squared error, a different loss.

t.zh: 类别很多时，除了看第一名是否正确（Top-1），还可以看正确类别是否在前五名里（Top-5）。例如正确答案排第二，Top-1 算错，Top-5 算对；两者回答的问题不同。
t.en: With many classes, we can check whether the top prediction is correct (top-1) or whether the correct class is among the top five (top-5). If the answer ranks second, top-1 counts it wrong and top-5 counts it right; they answer different questions.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：把三个分变成三个概率，规则在说明里。要想的问题：负的分该怎么办？
t.en: Your task in this level: turn the three scores into three probabilities, by the rule in the brief. Something to think about: what should happen to a negative score?

brief.zh: 分拣机要把零件分成三类：X、O 和 +。网络先给每类打一个分，S1、S2、S3 依次对应 X、O、+，分可正可负。把三个分变成三个概率：每个都在 0 到 1 之间，加起来是 1，分越高的概率越大。期望用的是 e^分 ÷ 三个 e^分 之和。
brief.en: The sorting machine has to put parts into three classes: X, O and +. The network first gives each class a score: S1, S2 and S3 correspond to X, O and +. Scores may be positive or negative. Turn the three scores into three probabilities, each between 0 and 1, adding up to 1, with a higher score getting a higher probability. The expected output uses e^score ÷ the sum of the three e^score.

hint.zh: 分可能是负数，直接除以总和会出错。exp 把任何数变成正数。
hint.en: Scores can be negative, so dividing by their sum goes wrong. exp turns any number positive.

after.zh: 这台分拣机把局部特征汇总成类别判断：卷积可以找不同的笔画，非线性和池化帮助处理位置变化，分类部分根据特征给各类打分。它在这些新零件上也通过了检查，说明它不只适用于训练例子；要了解它在实际使用中是否可靠，还需要更多有代表性的测试。
after.en: This sorting machine combines local features into a class decision: convolutions can find different strokes, nonlinearities and pooling help with changes in position, and the classifier scores each class from the features. Passing on these new parts shows it works beyond the training examples; assessing reliability in practice requires more representative tests.

t.zh: 分拣机正式上线：零件的位置、深浅都不一样，有的带噪点。最后几组是「新零件」，不参加训练，只用来检查。
t.en: The sorter goes live: parts sit in different places, at different strengths, some with noise. The last few sets are "new parts" that take no part in training and are only checked.

t.zh: 从图片到类别，网络先提取局部特征，再把特征汇总成类别分数。AlexNet 把卷积、激活、池化和分类层组合起来，用大量图片训练；这一关是缩小后的分类例子。
t.en: From image to class, a network first extracts local features and then combines them into class scores. AlexNet combined convolution, activation, pooling and classification layers and trained on many images; this level is a much smaller classification example.

t.zh: 换一批新零件时，不一定从零开始：可以复用已经训练好的特征提取部分，只训练新的分类头；如果旧特征不够适合，也可以解冻部分层继续训练，这叫微调。这里仍然从当前任务训练。
t.en: For a new set of parts, we do not always have to start from scratch: we can reuse a trained feature extractor and train only a new classification head. If the old features do not fit well enough, we can unfreeze some layers and train them further; this is fine-tuning. This level still trains on its current task.

t.zh: 如果通过了<level-ref to="4-20"></level-ref>，可以使用解锁的 Softmax 元件，把三类分数变成概率。也可以自己搭出这一步。
t.en: If you passed <level-ref to="4-20"></level-ref>, you can use the unlocked Softmax part to turn the three scores into probabilities. You can also build this step yourself.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：输出三个概率，正确那一类大于 0.55，另两类小于 0.45。要想的问题：三类零件靠哪些笔画区分？网络要看出几种笔画？
t.en: Your task in this level: output three probabilities, above 0.55 for the right class and below 0.45 for the other two. Something to think about: which strokes tell the three kinds apart? How many kinds of stroke must the network see?

brief.zh: 传送带上的零件有三种：X、O 和 +，位置、深浅都不一样，有的带噪点。输出三个概率，正确那一类要大于 0.55，另两类小于 0.45。列表最后的「新零件」不参加训练，只用来检查。
brief.en: The parts on the belt come in three kinds, X, O and +, at different places and strengths, some with noise. Output three probabilities: above 0.55 for the right class, below 0.45 for the other two. The "new parts" at the end of the list take no part in training and are only checked.

hint.zh: 一个卷积通道只能看出一种笔画，三类至少要几种？每一类的分，可以由每个通道的特征各给一点。搭好后多按几次训练，看两条误差线。
hint.en: One convolution channel can pick out only one kind of stroke; how many do three classes need at least? Each class's score can take a share from every channel's feature. Once built, train for a while and watch the two error lines.

title.en: Let the machine turn the knobs

after.zh: 你没有设计这个核，它是从例子里学出来的。手工设计的特征，就这样被学到的特征取代了。
after.en: You didn't design this kernel; it was learned from examples. This is how learned features replace hand-designed ones.

t.zh: <level-ref to="1-9"></level-ref>里，你看着输入和输出，一格格拧出了一个 3×3 核。那个核的数字很整齐，猜得出来。要是九个数乱七八糟、毫无规律呢？
t.en: In <level-ref to="1-9"></level-ref> you looked at the input and output and worked out a 3×3 kernel cell by cell. Its numbers were tidy enough to guess. What if the nine numbers are a jumble with no pattern at all?

t.zh: 新元件<part-ref to="part:learn3"></part-ref>：和 3×3 核一样拿九个权重去压图，只是权重不用你填，它会照着测试的期望自己调。<level-ref to="4-2"></level-ref>只有一两个旋钮，这次是九个。
t.en: The new part is <part-ref to="part:learn3"></part-ref>: like the 3×3 kernel, it presses nine weights over the image, but you do not fill in the weights; it tunes them itself to match the tests' expected outputs. <level-ref to="4-2"></level-ref> had one or two knobs; this time there are nine.

t.zh: 训练时先用当前参数算出结果，和答案比较得到损失，再根据每个参数对损失的影响更新参数。这里用微小改动估计影响；真实神经网络通常用反向传播，把损失的影响逐层传回去。
