t.en: Training first computes an output with the current parameters and compares it with the answer to obtain a loss. It then updates each parameter according to its effect on that loss. Here small changes estimate that effect; real neural networks usually use backpropagation to pass the effect of the loss backwards through the layers.

t.zh: 真实训练常把样本分成小批次：一批样本算一次更新；整个训练集遍历一遍叫一个 epoch（训练轮）。批次大小和训练轮数是训练安排，不是网络学到的权重。
t.en: Real training often divides samples into mini-batches: one batch contributes to an update; one pass through the training set is an epoch. Batch size and the number of epochs are training choices, not weights learned by the network.

t.zh: 这一关的输入是一片随机噪点，期望是某个没人告诉你的核压过它的结果。你要做的：让输出和期望对上。
t.en: The input in this level is random noise, and the expected output is what you get by pressing some kernel nobody tells you about over it. Your task: make the output match the expected.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：噪点 → 某个未知的核压过之后
caption.en: Set 1: noise → after an unknown kernel is pressed over it

brief.zh: 在<level-ref to="4-2"></level-ref>里，你用一个、两个旋钮下过山。这次是一个未知的 3×3 核：九个旋钮，数字很乱，凭眼睛猜不出来。接上可学习核，按「训练」。
brief.en: In <level-ref to="4-2"></level-ref> you walked downhill with one knob, then two. This time it is an unknown 3×3 kernel: nine knobs with messy numbers you can't guess by eye. Wire up a learnable kernel and press "Train".

hint.zh: 每按一次，九个旋钮一起往下坡挪一步（和<level-ref to="4-1"></level-ref>、<level-ref to="4-2"></level-ref>一样，只是旋钮多了）。看损失曲线往下走。
hint.en: Each press moves all nine knobs one step downhill together (just as in <level-ref to="4-1"></level-ref> and <level-ref to="4-2"></level-ref>, only with more knobs). Watch the loss curve go down.

after.zh: 从几对例子里学到的核，换成没见过的照片照样对：这才是学会了，而不是背下了。训练面板里，训练误差是在用来学的样本上算的，新样本误差是在没给它看过的样本上算的。后面判断一个模型好不好，看的都是后者。
after.en: A kernel learned from a few example pairs works just as well on photos it has never seen: that is learning, not memorising. In the training panel, the training error is measured on the samples it learns from, and the new-sample error on samples it was never shown. From now on, a model is judged by the second.

t.zh: 相机按快门时手一抖，照片就糊了一下。每台相机抖的样子都差不多，可没人知道具体是什么样。
t.en: If the hand shakes as the shutter clicks, the photo blurs a little. Each camera shakes in much the same way, but nobody knows exactly how.

t.zh: 这一关给你几对照片：清楚的原图和这台相机拍出来的样子。最后两组是「新照片」：它们不参加训练，只用来检查学到的东西对没见过的照片管不管用。训练面板会多画一条新样本的误差线。
t.en: This level gives you a few pairs of photos: the sharp original and what this camera captured. The last two sets are "new photos": they take no part in training and only check whether what was learned works on photos it has never seen. The training panel draws an extra error line for the new samples.

caption.zh: 第一组：字母 F 和抖过的样子
caption.en: Set 1: the letter F and how it came out shaken

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：训练一个可学习核，学会这台相机的抖。
t.en: Your task in this level: train a learnable kernel to learn this camera's shake.

brief.zh: 一台相机拍照时总会抖一下。给你几对照片：清楚的原图和这台相机拍出的样子。训练一个可学习核学会这种抖，最后几张「新照片」不参加训练，只用来检查学到的核对新照片也对。
brief.en: A camera always shakes a little as it takes a photo. Here are a few pairs: the sharp original and how this camera captures it. Train a learnable kernel to learn the shake. The last few "new photos" take no part in training and are only used to check that the learned kernel works on new photos too.

hint.zh: 和<level-ref to="4-3"></level-ref>一样，只是这次的图是真实的照片。看训练面板里的两条误差线。
hint.en: The same as <level-ref to="4-3"></level-ref>, only this time the pictures are real photos. Watch the two error lines in the training panel.

after.zh: 加权和再压一下，就是一个神经元。w1·斜 + w2·弯 + b = 0 是平面上的一条直线，神经元在它的一侧说「是」，另一侧说「不是」：一个神经元就是一条分界线。1 / (1 + e^(−z)) 这道压缩叫 Sigmoid。
after.en: A weighted sum and then a squash: that is a neuron. w1·diagonal + w2·curved + b = 0 is a straight line in the plane, and the neuron says "yes" on one side and "no" on the other: one neuron is one dividing line. The squash 1 / (1 + e^(−z)) is called the sigmoid.

t.zh: 「神经网络」的名字来自大脑：神经细胞收到许多信号，合起来够强就兴奋。计算机里的神经元是它的简化版，一个只做一件小事的计算单元。
t.en: The name "neural network" comes from the brain: a nerve cell receives many signals and fires when together they are strong enough. A neuron in a computer is a simplified version, a computing unit that does one small thing.

t.zh: 每组测试是一张字母图，已经缩成两个数：斜笔画多少、弯笔画多少。于是一张图就是平面上的一个点，神经元要给每个点打一个分。
t.en: Each test is a letter picture already reduced to two numbers: how much diagonal stroke and how much curved stroke. So a picture is a point in the plane, and the neuron gives each point a score.

t.zh: 新元件 exp 把每个数 x 换成 e 的 x 次方：x 越大越大，x 是负数时接近 0，但永远是正的。
t.en: The new part exp replaces each number x with e to the power x: the bigger x, the bigger it gets; for negative x it approaches 0 but stays positive.

caption.zh: exp 处理一条从 0 到 1 的斜坡
caption.en: exp on a ramp from 0 to 1

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：按说明搭出神经元，训练它分开 X 和 O。要想的问题：只靠这三个可学习的数，它能分开哪些点，又分不开哪些？
t.en: Your task in this level: build the neuron as the brief describes and train it to separate X from O. Something to think about: with only these three learnable numbers, which points can it separate, and which can it not?

brief.zh: 每组测试是一张字母图，已经缩成两个数：斜笔画多少、弯笔画多少。搭一个神经元：两个数各乘一个可学习的权重，加起来再加一个可学习的偏置 z，最后用 1 / (1 + e^(−z)) 把它压到 0 和 1 之间。训练它：X 输出大于 0.6，O 小于 0.4。
brief.en: Each test is a letter picture already reduced to two numbers: how much diagonal stroke and how much curved stroke. Build a neuron: multiply each number by a learnable weight, add them up and add a learnable bias z, then squash it between 0 and 1 with 1 / (1 + e^(−z)). Train it: above 0.6 for X, below 0.4 for O.

hint.zh: 新元件 exp 算 e 的几次方。
hint.en: The new part exp raises e to a power.

after.zh: 一条直线怎么摆都分不开异或。两个神经元先各画一条线，把每个点变成两个新的数，输出神经元在新的坐标里一条线就够了：这就是隐藏层。还有一件事：几个神经元一开始完全一样，训练时每一步的变化也一样，永远学不出不同的东西，所以网络的权重要从不同的随机数开始。
after.en: However you place one straight line, it cannot separate exclusive-or. Let two neurons each draw a line first, turning every point into two new numbers, and in these new coordinates the output neuron needs just one line: that is a hidden layer. One more thing: if several neurons start out identical, every training step changes them identically and they can never learn different things. That is why a network's weights start from different random numbers.

t.zh: <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>的 X 和 O 在平面上各占一边。这一关换了规则：X 是「只有一种笔画」，O 是「两种都有，或者都没有」。
t.en: <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>'s X and O each sat on one side of the plane. This level changes the rule: X means "only one kind of stroke", O means "both kinds, or neither".

t.zh: <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref>搭的 1 / (1 + e^(−z)) 现在是现成的元件<part-ref to="sigmoid"></part-ref>。
t.en: The 1 / (1 + e^(−z)) you built in <level-ref to="4-5"></level-ref> is now the ready-made part <part-ref to="sigmoid"></part-ref>.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：X 输出大于 0.6，O 小于 0.4。要想的问题：一个神经元是一条分界线，这些点能被一条直线分开吗？
t.en: Your task in this level: above 0.6 for X, below 0.4 for O. Something to think about: one neuron is one dividing line; can these points be split by a straight line?

brief.zh: 换了一批字母：X 是「只有一种笔画」（斜多弯少，或弯多斜少），O 是「两种都多，或者都少」。X 输出大于 0.6，O 小于 0.4。
brief.en: A new batch of letters: X means "only one kind of stroke" (more diagonal than curved, or the other way round), O means "both kinds a lot, or both a little". Above 0.6 for X, below 0.4 for O.

hint.zh: 先试一个神经元，在纸上画画这些点：一条直线分得开吗？神经元的输出，也可以交给另一个神经元。几个神经元一开始的权重一模一样的话，训练能让它们变得不一样吗？
hint.en: Try one neuron first, and sketch the points on paper: can a straight line separate them? A neuron's output can be fed to another neuron. If several neurons start with exactly the same weights, can training ever make them differ?

after.zh: 任何只含加、减和乘常数的组合都是线性的，正负号必然对称。「负数变 0、正数不变」叫 ReLU。中间插一个非线性，网络才能表达「两种都要」。这就是神经网络需要激活函数的原因。
after.en: Any combination of adding, subtracting and multiplying by constants is linear, so the signs are bound to be symmetric. "Negatives become 0, positives stay" is called ReLU. Only with a nonlinearity in between can a network express "I want both". This is why neural networks need activation functions.

t.zh: 你用差分找过台阶：暗→亮是正，亮→暗是负，符号还能告诉你边朝哪边。可很多时候只关心「这里有没有边」，不在乎方向。
t.en: You found steps with a difference: dark→bright is positive, bright→dark negative, and the sign even tells you which way the edge faces. But often all that matters is "is there an edge here", whatever its direction.

t.zh: 回忆一下横向差分：一个亮方块的左右两条边，一条是正的，一条是负的。这一关要两条都变成正的强度。
t.en: Recall the horizontal difference: of a bright square's left and right edges, one comes out positive and the other negative. In this level both have to become positive strengths.

caption.zh: 横向差分处理亮方块：两侧一正一负
caption.en: Horizontal difference on a bright square: one side positive, the other negative

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：不管是变亮还是变暗，每条竖边都输出它的强度。先看清第一组的输入和期望。
t.en: Your task: for every vertical edge, whether it goes brighter or darker, output its strength. Look carefully at the input and expected output of Set 1 first.

caption.zh: 第一组测试：亮方块 → 两条边都是正的
caption.en: Set 1: bright square → both edges positive

brief.zh: 暗→亮的边和亮→暗的边都要输出正的强度（输出 = |右边 − 自己|）。
brief.en: Both dark→light and light→dark edges must give a positive strength (output = |right − self|).

hint.zh: 只用加、减和乘常数，无论怎么组合，暗→亮和亮→暗都会得到相反的符号。有没有办法只留下正的部分？
hint.en: With only adding, subtracting and multiplying by constants, however you combine them, dark→light and light→dark get opposite signs. Is there a way to keep only the positive part?

after.zh: max(a, b) = b + ReLU(a − b)：a 大就补上多出的那一截，b 大就什么也不补。
after.en: max(a, b) = b + ReLU(a − b): if a is bigger, add the amount it is bigger by; if b is bigger, add nothing.

t.zh: 托盘里的 ReLU 让负数变 0、正数不变。
t.en: The ReLU in the tray turns negatives into 0 and leaves positives as they are.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：两张图逐格比较，每格输出较大的那个。要想的问题：a 比 b 大多少？这个差什么时候是正的？
t.en: Your task in this level: compare two pictures cell by cell and output the larger value in each. Something to think about: how much bigger is a than b? When is that difference positive?

caption.en: Set 1: a square and a disc

brief.zh: 两张图逐格比较，每格输出较大的那个：max(a, b)。
brief.en: Compare two pictures cell by cell and output the larger value in each: max(a, b).

hint.zh: ReLU 留下正的部分。a 比 b 大多少？
hint.en: ReLU keeps the positive part. How much bigger is a than b?

after.zh: 步幅为 2，输出就隔一个取一个。一般地，输出边长 = ⌊(N + 2p − k) / s⌋ + 1：N 是输入边长，k 是窗口大小，p 是补边宽度，s 是步幅。这一层只有 9 个要学的数，图变大变小都一样，因为同一组权重在每个位置都用：这叫权重共享。看评分里的「参数」。
after.en: With a stride of 2, the output keeps every other position. In general, output width = ⌊(N + 2p − k) / s⌋ + 1, with N the input width, k the window size, p the padding and s the stride. This layer has only 9 numbers to learn, however big or small the picture, because the same weights are used at every position: this is called weight sharing. See "Parameters" in the score.

t.zh: 到现在为止，元件的输出都和输入一样大。真正的卷积网络里，图往往一层层变小：一张照片几百万个像素，缩小之后，后面的层才算得动。
t.en: So far every part's output has been as big as its input. In a real convolutional network the picture usually shrinks layer by layer: a photo has millions of pixels, and only after shrinking can the later layers keep up.

t.zh: 卷积层的窗口就是你熟悉的 3×3 核：停在图上一处，算出一个数，再挪到下一处。每次挪几格，叫步幅。
t.en: A convolution layer's window is the familiar 3×3 kernel: it stops at one place, works out a number, then moves on. How far it moves each time is the stride.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：做出一层步幅为 2 的卷积，权重由训练找出来。测试图有两种大小。要想的问题：图变大时，这一层要学的数会不会跟着变多？
t.en: Your task in this level: make a convolution layer with stride 2, with its weights found by training. The test pictures come in two sizes. Something to think about: when the picture gets bigger, does this layer have more numbers to learn?

caption.zh: 第一组：字母 F，输出只有一半大
caption.en: Set 1: the letter F, with an output half the size

brief.zh: 一层卷积的窗口每次挪两格，输出边长只有输入的一半。窗口里的 3×3 权重不知道，要训练出来。测试图有 16×16 的，也有 12×12 的：同一个电路都要对。
brief.en: A convolution layer whose window moves two pixels at a time, so the output is half the input's width. The 3×3 weights in the window are unknown and have to be trained. Some test pictures are 16×16 and some 12×12: the same circuit must be right for both.

hint.zh: 窗口每次挪两格，等于先在每个位置都算一遍，再隔一个留一个。
hint.en: Moving the window two pixels at a time is the same as computing at every position and then keeping every other one.

after.zh: 查询 Q 与键 K 的比较决定权重，值 V 提供被加权汇总的内容。这里使用缩放点积和 Softmax 计算权重；真实视觉模型通常学习 Q、K、V 的特征表示，让各个图块汇总有用的信息。
after.en: Comparisons between query Q and keys K determine the weights; values V provide the information being combined. This experiment uses scaled dot products and Softmax for the weights. Vision models usually learn the Q, K and V representations so each patch can combine useful information.

t.zh: 卷积一次处理局部区域；注意力可以让一个图块汇总来自其他图块的信息。先通过三段实验观察它如何选择信息、如何形成输出。
t.en: A convolution processes a local region at a time; attention lets a patch combine information from other patches. Three experiments show how attention selects information and forms an output.

t.zh: 图中有一个查询 Q、两个键 K 和对应的值 V。Q 与两个 K 分别比较，得到两个权重；这两个权重用于汇总对应的 V。
t.en: The experiment has one query Q, two keys K and their corresponding values V. Q is compared with both keys to obtain two weights, which are used to combine the corresponding values.

t.zh: 本实验用 4×4 的像素图块直接表示 Q、K 和 V。真实视觉模型通常先将图块变成特征，并用可学习的投影生成 Q、K、V。
t.en: This experiment uses 4×4 pixel patches directly as Q, K and V. Vision models usually first turn patches into features and use learned projections to produce Q, K and V.

brief.zh: 切换查询 Q，比较两个键的权重怎样变化。然后将 Q 设为 O，选择权重较大的键。
brief.en: Switch query Q and compare how the weights of the two keys change. Then set Q to O and select the key with the greater weight.

hint.zh: 键 A 是 X，键 B 是 O。查询与每个键分别比较，匹配程度影响对应的权重。
hint.en: Key A is X and key B is O. The query is compared with each key; the match affects the corresponding weight.

status.en: Adjust the patches and select an answer.

after.zh: Q 是当前图块用于寻找相关信息的表示。改变 Q，即使候选键不变，分配给各个值的权重也会变化。
after.en: Q represents the current patch when finding relevant information. Changing Q can change the weights assigned to the values even when the candidate keys stay fixed.

brief.zh: 查询 Q 固定为 X。交换键 A、B，观察权重如何变化，选择交换后权重较大的键。值的位置保持不变。
brief.en: Query Q is fixed as X. Swap keys A and B, observe the weights, and select the key with the greater weight after the swap. The values stay in place.

hint.zh: 键用于与查询比较；每个键的权重会分配给同一位置的值。
hint.en: Keys are compared with the query; each key’s weight is assigned to the value in the same position.

status.en: Adjust the patches and select an answer.

after.zh: K 是候选信息用于匹配的表示。改变 K 会改变分数和权重，也会改变对应位置的 V 对输出的贡献。
after.en: K represents candidate information for matching. Changing K changes the scores and weights, and therefore the contribution of the V at the corresponding position.

brief.zh: 查询和键保持不变。交换值 A、B，观察权重和输出图块，选择输出中更明显的图案。
brief.en: Keep the query and keys fixed. Swap values A and B, observe the weights and output patch, and select the more prominent pattern in the output.

hint.zh: 权重由 Q 和 K 决定；输出的每个像素是两个值在对应位置的加权和。
hint.en: Q and K determine the weights; each output pixel is the weighted sum of the corresponding pixels in the two values.

status.en: Adjust the patches and select an answer.

after.zh: 被擦的那块和远处的孪生块最像，于是一步就从对角取回了缺的格子。这就是自注意力：每个图块（token）用 q·k/√d 和所有图块打分，softmax 把分数变成和为 1 的权重，再对 v 加权平均。3×3 卷积叠 L 层也只看到 (2L+1)×(2L+1)。
after.en: The erased patch looks most like its far-off twin, so in one step it fetched the missing pixels from the opposite corner. That is self-attention: each patch (token) scores every patch with q·k/√d, softmax turns the scores into weights that sum to 1, and the v are averaged with those weights. Stack L layers of 3×3 convolution and you still only see (2L+1)×(2L+1).

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="attention"></part-ref>把 16×16 的图切成 16 个 4×4 的图块，每块都向所有图块提问。参数「q 放大」把分数一起放大：放得越大，越只看最像的几块。
t.en: The <part-ref to="attention"></part-ref> in the tray cuts the 16×16 image into 16 patches of 4×4, and every patch asks every patch. The "q scale" parameter scales up all the scores: the larger it is, the more each patch looks only at the few most alike.

t.zh: 测试图的一对对角上本是同一个小图案，其中一个被擦掉几格；也有一组什么都没擦。这一关最多 3 个节点。要想的是：被擦掉的格子，图里哪里还留着它的样子？
t.en: In each test image, two opposite corners hold the same small pattern, but one has had a few pixels erased; one set has nothing erased. This level allows at most 3 nodes. The question is: where else in the image does an erased pixel still show what it looked like?

caption.zh: 第一组：左上角的图案缺了几格
caption.en: Set 1: the top-left pattern is missing a few pixels

brief.zh: 一对对角上本是同一个图案，其中一个被擦掉了几格。把它补回来，其余不变；最多 3 个节点。
brief.en: Two opposite corners hold the same pattern, but a few pixels of one copy have been erased. Restore them and leave everything else unchanged; at most 3 nodes.

hint.zh: 3×3 的元件一次只看一格远。注意力让每个图块和所有图块比；q 放大越大，越只看最像的几块。
hint.en: A 3×3 part only sees one pixel away at a time. Attention lets each patch compare itself with every patch; the larger the q scale, the more it looks only at the few most similar ones.

after.zh: 图块数 = 像素数 ÷ P²，注意力的计算量跟着图块数涨；图块大了，每块又粗得只能认出大结构。ViT 把 224×224 的图切成 16×16 的图块，正好是 196 个：在计算量和细节之间取的一个折中。
after.en: The number of patches is the number of pixels ÷ P², and the cost of attention grows with it; but bigger patches are too coarse to see anything but large structure. ViT cuts a 224×224 image into 16×16 patches, exactly 196 of them: a compromise between cost and detail.

t.zh: 注意力里，每一格都要把所有图块加一遍。图块切得越小，图块就越多，要算的也越多。
t.en: In attention, every cell adds up over all the patches. The smaller the patches, the more of them there are, and the more there is to compute.

t.zh: <part-ref to="attention"></part-ref>多了一个设置：图块边长 P，可以是 2、4 或 8。
t.en: <part-ref to="attention"></part-ref> has gained a setting: the patch size P, which can be 2, 4 or 8.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：图案变成了 8×8 的，一张图四个，还是补全对角；计算量有上限。
t.en: Your task in this level: the patterns are now 8×8, four to a picture, and it is mending across the diagonal again; the cost has a limit.

caption.zh: 第一组：左上角的图案缺了几块
caption.en: Set 1: the top-left pattern is missing a few blocks

brief.zh: 还是补全对角，这次图案是 8×8 的，一张图四个。计算量不能超过 10。
brief.en: Mending across the diagonal again, this time with 8×8 patterns, four to a picture. The cost must not exceed 10.

hint.zh: 注意力的每一格都要把所有图块加一遍。图块越大，图块越少。
hint.en: Each cell of attention adds up over every patch. The bigger the patches, the fewer there are.

after.zh: 每个注意力只能按一种相似去找。多头注意力并排放几个注意力，各自用自己的 Q、K 找一种关系，再把结果拼在一起。Transformer 的每一层都有好几个头。
after.en: Each attention can only look for one kind of likeness. Multi-head attention puts several side by side, each finding one kind of relation with its own Q and K, and then puts their results together. Every layer of a Transformer has several heads.

t.zh: 一个注意力按一种「像」去找：Q 和 K 从哪张图来，它就按那张图比。
t.en: One attention looks for one kind of likeness: whichever picture Q and K come from, that is the picture it compares by.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：两张图各有一个图案被擦掉几格，孪生图案在各自图里的别处。两个输出分别补好两张图。
t.en: Your task in this level: each of two pictures has a pattern with a few pixels erased, and its twin is elsewhere in the same picture. The two outputs are the two pictures mended.

brief.zh: 两张图各有一个图案被擦掉几格，它的孪生图案在同一张图的别处。两个输出分别是补好的两张图。
brief.en: Each of two pictures has one pattern with a few pixels erased; its twin is elsewhere in the same picture. The two outputs are the two pictures mended.

hint.zh: 一个注意力只按一种「像」去找。两张图里的孪生关系一样吗？
hint.en: One attention looks for one kind of likeness. Do the twins pair up the same way in both pictures?

after.zh: 没有位置时，把两个图块对调，注意力的输出也只是跟着对调：它看到的是一袋图块，不是一串。你给每个图块加上了它的编号乘一个小数：这叫位置编码 z̃ᵢ = zᵢ + pᵢ，每个图块带着自己的地址，顺序才进得了计算。ViT 在进入第一层之前就把位置加到每个图块上。
after.en: Without position, swap two patches and attention's output just swaps with them: it sees a bag of patches, not a sequence. You added each patch's number times a small amount: this is a positional encoding z̃ᵢ = zᵢ + pᵢ, so every patch carries its own address and order can enter the computation. ViT adds the position to every patch before the first layer.

t.zh: 「狗咬人」和「人咬狗」用的是同样的字，意思却相反，差别全在顺序。图也一样：左边亮右边暗，和反过来，是两张不同的图。
t.en: "Dog bites man" and "man bites dog" use the same words but mean opposite things; the difference is all in the order. Images are the same: bright on the left and dark on the right is a different image from the reverse.

t.zh: <level-ref to="5-1"></level-ref>的注意力按「长得像不像」分配权重，它清楚每个图块是什么样子。可它知道这块排在第几吗？先想一想：把两个图块对调，注意力的输出会怎样？
t.en: The attention from <level-ref to="5-1"></level-ref> shares out its weights by how alike patches look, so it knows what each patch looks like. But does it know where a patch comes in the order? Think first: if you swap two patches, what happens to the attention output?

t.zh: 这一关多了一个输入：每一格所在图块的编号，按阅读顺序从 0 数到 15。
t.en: This level has an extra input: the number of the patch each cell is in, counting 0 to 15 in reading order.

t.zh: 测试图是一片灰，里面有一块亮、一块暗。按先左后右、再从上到下的顺序，亮块在前就整张输出 1，否则输出 0。测试是成对的：同样两块，只换了位置。
t.en: Each test image is grey with one bright patch and one dark patch. Reading left to right, then top to bottom, output 1 everywhere if the bright patch comes first, otherwise 0. The tests come in pairs: the same two patches with their positions swapped.

caption.zh: 亮块是第 2 块，暗块是第 3 块：亮在前，期望全是 1
caption.en: The bright patch is number 2 and the dark one number 3: bright comes first, so expect all 1s

brief.zh: 按阅读顺序（先左后右，再从上到下），亮块排在暗块前面就整张图输出 1，否则输出 0。第二个输入是每格所在图块的编号 0 … 15。
brief.en: In reading order (left to right, then top to bottom), if the bright patch comes before the dark one, output 1 over the whole image; otherwise output 0. The second input is the number of the patch each pixel is in, 0 … 15.

hint.zh: Q、K 决定看谁，V 决定带回什么。要让结果知道亮块和暗块各在哪儿，位置该从哪一路进来？
hint.en: Q and K decide whom to look at; V decides what comes back. For the result to know where the bright and dark patches sit, which input should carry the position?

after.zh: 所有图块用同一个查询（全 1）去问，分数就只看每块的总和，大家都看向同一块。ViT 在图块前面多放一个可学习的 [CLS] 图块，它的查询经过训练，专门替整张图提问，分类时只读它的输出。
after.en: When every patch asks with the same query (all ones), the score depends only on each patch's total, and they all look at the same patch. ViT puts an extra learnable [CLS] patch in front of the others; its query is trained to ask on behalf of the whole picture, and only its output is read to classify.

t.zh: 自注意力里，每个图块都用自己去提问，所以各问各的。
t.en: In self-attention every patch asks with itself, so each asks its own question.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：每个图块都换成全图最亮的那个图块，也就是各格加起来最大的那一块。
t.en: Your task in this level: replace every patch with the brightest patch in the picture, the one whose cells add up to the most.

brief.zh: 每个图块都换成全图最亮（各格加起来最大）的那个图块。
brief.en: Replace every patch with the brightest patch in the picture (the one whose cells add up to the most).

hint.zh: 自注意力里，每块用自己去提问。要是每块问的是同一个问题呢？
hint.en: In self-attention, each patch asks with itself. What if every patch asked the same question?

after.zh: 只拉近正对时，把所有图都放到同一点就能让损失最小，却什么也分不出：这叫坍缩。InfoNCE 的分母把同一批里的其他视图当作负对推开，点才在圆上散开。变形本身提供了答案，不需要人工标签：这就是自监督的对比学习（SimCLR）。
after.en: When only positive pairs are pulled together, putting every image at the same point minimises the loss but tells nothing apart: this is called collapse. InfoNCE's denominator treats the other views in the batch as negative pairs and pushes them away, so the dots spread out round the circle. The alterations themselves supply the answer, with no human labels: this is self-supervised contrastive learning (SimCLR).

t.zh: 前几章的训练都靠标签：每张图配一个人写的答案。可现实里绝大多数照片没有标签，给上百万张图逐一标注又贵又慢。没有答案，还能学吗？
t.en: Training in earlier chapters relied on labels: every image came with an answer written by a person. But in the real world almost no photos have labels, and labelling millions of images one by one is slow and expensive. Can a model still learn without answers?

t.zh: 一个办法：把一张图做成两个变形版本，挪一点、调亮暗、加点噪声。两个版本一定来自同一张图，这件事本身就能当答案用。很多图像模型先这样在大量没标签的图上练过。
t.en: One way: make two altered versions of an image, shifted a little, brighter or darker, with some noise added. The two versions are certain to come from the same image, and that fact alone can serve as the answer. Many image models are first trained like this on huge numbers of unlabelled images.

t.zh: 台上的编码器把每个视图变成一个方向，画成圆上的一个点；同一张图的两个视图连着线，叫一对搭档。测验时，每个视图要在所有点里挑出自己的搭档。
t.en: The encoder on the bench turns each view into a direction, drawn as a point on a circle; the two views of the same image are joined by a line and called a pair of partners. In the quiz, each view has to pick out its own partner from all the points.

t.zh: 损失公式分两项：一项把搭档拉近，一项把同一批里的其他视图推开，第二项可以开关。这一关你要训练编码器。动手前先想：一个好的编码器，点在圆上应该是什么样子？
t.en: The loss has two terms: one pulls partners together, the other pushes away the other views in the same batch, and the second can be switched on or off. In this level you train the encoder. Before you start, think: with a good encoder, what should the points on the circle look like?

brief.zh: 没有标签，只有每张图的两个变形版本。训练编码器，让测验里的每个视图都以 ≥ 50% 的概率认出自己的搭档。
brief.en: No labels, only two altered versions of each image. Train the encoder so that every view in the quiz picks out its partner with probability ≥ 50%.

hint.zh: 只拉近搭档，最省事的办法是什么？看看所有点最后去了哪里。
hint.en: If you only pull partners together, what is the laziest way to do it? Watch where all the dots end up.

label.en: Lowest chance of picking the partner
Mean sim of negative pairs, no collapse

text.zh: 嵌入平面 · 测验视图
● 第 1 个视图　○ 第 2 个视图　— 连线连接同一张图的两个视图
text.en: ● First view  ○ Second view  — A line joins the two views of the same image

after.zh: 编码器把同一张图的各种变形放到特征空间里相近的地方，再按余弦相似度找最近的一个：这就是以图搜图。对比学习练出来的编码器，正好适合这件事。
after.en: The encoder puts the different versions of one picture close together in feature space; then the nearest one by cosine similarity is found. This is image search, and an encoder trained by contrastive learning is just right for it.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="embed"></part-ref>把一张图变成一组特征，同一张图的各种变形得到的特征很接近。
t.en: The <part-ref to="embed"></part-ref> in the tray turns a picture into a set of features, and different versions of the same picture get features close to each other.

t.zh: 两组特征有多像，可以用余弦相似度来量：长度为 1 的两组特征，对应相乘再加起来。
t.en: How alike two sets of features are can be measured by cosine similarity: for two sets of features of length 1, multiply them pair by pair and add up.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：三张候选里找出和要找的照片是同一张的那一张。
t.en: Your task in this level: among three candidates, find the one that is the same photo as the one you are looking for.

brief.zh: 三张候选里有一张和要找的是同一张照片，只是挪了一点、调了颜色或加了噪声。是它的那一路输出 1，其余输出 0。
brief.en: One of the three candidates is the same photo as the one to find, only shifted a little, recoloured or noisy. Output 1 on its line and 0 on the others.

hint.zh: 逐像素比，亮的陌生人反而显得近。先把每张照片换成编码器的特征再比。
hint.en: Compared pixel by pixel, a bright stranger looks closer. Turn every photo into the encoder's features before comparing.

after.zh: 编码、算余弦、过门槛：相册去重、以图搜图、人脸验证都是这条流水线，差别在编码器学的是哪种「同一个」。门槛定高了会漏掉重复，定低了会把不同的照片并在一起。
after.en: Encode, take the cosine, apply a threshold: album clean-up, image search and face verification are all this pipeline, differing in what kind of "same" the encoder has learnt. Set the threshold too high and duplicates slip through; too low and different photos get merged.

t.zh: 相册里常有同一张照片的好几个版本：裁过的、调过色的、压缩出噪点的。整理相册时要把它们并成一张，不同的照片却不能并。
t.en: An album often holds several versions of the same photo: cropped, recoloured, noisy from compression. Tidying the album means merging them into one, but different photos must not be merged.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：两张照片是同一张就输出 1，否则输出 0。
t.en: Your task in this level: output 1 if the two photos are the same photo, otherwise 0.

brief.zh: 相册要合并重复的照片：挪了位置、调了颜色、加了噪声的同一张照片输出 1，不同的照片输出 0。
brief.en: The album wants to merge duplicate photos: output 1 for the same photo, even shifted, recoloured or noisy, and 0 for different photos.

hint.zh: 找近邻时你比较过相似度。这次没有候选可比，要自己定一条线。
hint.en: In nearest neighbour you compared similarities. This time there are no candidates to compare with, so you have to draw the line yourself.

after.zh: 你搭出了 Harris 角点检测：两个方向的变化都大，才是角。直边只有一个方向大，所以 det 小、R 为负。
after.en: You have built the Harris corner detector: it is a corner only when the change is large in both directions. A straight edge is large in only one direction, so det is small and R is negative.

t.zh: 手机拍全景时，要在相邻两张照片里认出同一个点，才能把它们拼齐。可不是每个点都好认：白墙上随便一点，换到墙上别处看起来也一样。
t.en: When a phone shoots a panorama, it has to recognise the same point in two neighbouring photos to line them up. But not every point is easy to recognise: any spot on a white wall looks just like any other spot on it.

t.zh: 这一章要回答：哪些点容易再找到？先比一比平坦处、直边、角这三种地方，想想各自是什么让它好认，或者难认。
t.en: This chapter asks: which points are easy to find again? Start by comparing three kinds of place, flat areas, straight edges and corners, and think about what makes each one easy or hard to recognise.

t.zh: Sobel x、Sobel y 你见过，分别量左右和上下方向的变化。<part-ref to="part:arith"></part-ref>选 ×，就把两张图逐格相乘。
t.en: You have met Sobel x and Sobel y: they measure change left-to-right and top-to-bottom. Set <part-ref to="part:arith"></part-ref> to × and it multiplies two images pixel by pixel.

t.zh: 测试有一个角、一个方块、一条直边和字母 L。角上输出 1，直边和平坦处都输出 0。少数格子出错可以接受。
t.en: The tests are a corner, a square, a straight edge and the letter L. Output 1 on corners and 0 on straight edges and flat areas. A few wrong pixels are fine.

caption.en: A corner: only the corner itself is 1

brief.zh: 只在角上输出 1。直边、平坦处都是 0。
brief.en: Output 1 only at corners. Straight edges and flat areas are 0.

hint.zh: 在角上，往哪个方向挪都会变；在直边上，沿着边挪不会变。分别统计 Gx²、Gy²、Gx·Gy 在 3×3 窗口里的和，再算 det − 0.05·trace²。
hint.en: At a corner, moving in any direction changes what you see; on a straight edge, moving along the edge changes nothing. Sum Gx², Gy² and Gx·Gy over a 3×3 window, then compute det − 0.05·trace².

after.zh: SIFT 描述子把关键点周围分成 4×4 个小格，每格做一个 8 个方向的直方图，一共 128 个数。方向按梯度分，幅值当票数：边往哪个方向变亮，这一格就往那个方向投票。
after.en: A SIFT descriptor divides the area round a keypoint into 4×4 small cells and makes an 8-direction histogram in each, 128 numbers in all. Directions follow the gradient and the magnitude is the vote: whichever way an edge brightens, the cell votes that way.

t.zh: 一个点光知道「在哪」还不够，还要记下它周围长什么样，才认得出。SIFT 的办法是数一数周围的边都朝哪个方向。
t.en: Knowing where a point is is not enough to recognise it; you also need to record what its surroundings look like. SIFT does it by counting which way the edges around it face.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：把每一格的梯度幅值分到上下左右四个方向，输出四个方向各自的平均。
t.en: Your task in this level: share each cell's gradient magnitude out to the four directions up, down, left and right, and output the average for each.

brief.zh: 把每一格的梯度幅值分给它最接近的方向：横向分量更大时，往右变亮算「→」，往左算「←」；纵向分量更大时，往下变亮算「↓」，往上算「↑」。四个输出是四个方向各自的幅值总和除以格数。
brief.en: Give each cell's gradient magnitude to the direction it is closest to: when the across part is larger, brightening to the right counts as "→" and to the left as "←"; when the down part is larger, brightening downwards counts as "↓" and upwards as "↑". The four outputs are the magnitude summed per direction, divided by the number of cells.

hint.zh: |gx| 是 gx 和 −gx 里较大的那个。每个方向是两个条件同时成立：哪个分量大，它的正负号。
hint.en: |gx| is the larger of gx and −gx. Each direction needs two conditions at once: which part is larger, and its sign.

after.zh: 单应矩阵 H 有 8 个自由度，每对点给 2 个方程，所以至少要 4 对点，游戏用 DLT 从你的点对解出了 H。3 对点只能定出仿射（6 个自由度），它保持平行，贴不上透视下的书。实际流水线里，这些点对来自距离比检验后的候选，再由 RANSAC 反复抽 4 对、数内点选出来。
after.en: The homography H has 8 degrees of freedom and each pair of points gives 2 equations, so it needs at least 4 pairs; the game solved H from your pairs with DLT. Three pairs only fix an affine map (6 degrees of freedom), which keeps lines parallel and cannot fit a book seen in perspective. In a real pipeline the pairs come from candidates that passed the ratio test, and RANSAC picks them by repeatedly drawing 4 pairs and counting inliers.

t.zh: 用手机对着一本书拍，App 能认出是哪本书，还能把封面图贴回照片里，增强现实（AR）常这样做。难处在于书是斜着拍的，在照片里不再方方正正。
t.en: Point your phone at a book and an app can tell which book it is and even paste the cover image back into the photo; augmented reality (AR) often works like this. The hard part is that the book is shot at an angle, so in the photo it is no longer a neat rectangle.

t.zh: 把封面贴回照片，需要一个变换：它告诉封面上的每个点，落到照片的哪里。变换由几对对应点算出来，点对给得合适，就贴得准。
t.en: Pasting the cover back into the photo needs a transformation: it tells each point on the cover where it lands in the photo. The transformation is computed from a few pairs of corresponding points; choose the pairs well and the cover lands accurately.

t.zh: 台上左边是封面，右边是照片。从封面上的一个点连到照片里同一个点，游戏会用你给的点对算出变换，把封面贴上去，并显示平均误差。
t.en: On the bench the cover is on the left and the photo on the right. Connect a point on the cover to the same point in the photo; the game computes the transformation from your point pairs, pastes the cover on and shows the average error.

t.zh: 这一关要把封面贴准，平均误差小于 1.5 像素。动手前先看看照片里书的形状：和封面原来的长方形比，变了哪些？
t.en: In this level you must paste the cover accurately, with an average error under 1.5 pixels. Before you start, look at the shape of the book in the photo: compared with the cover's original rectangle, what has changed?

brief.zh: 从封面上的点拖到照片里同一个点，连出对应点对。把封面贴回照片，平均误差小于 1.5 像素即通过。
brief.en: Drag from a point on the cover to the same point in the photo to make a pair of corresponding points. The cover is pasted back onto the photo; you pass when the mean error is under 1.5 pixels.

hint.zh: 贴回去的封面哪里对不上？斜着拍的书，远的一边更短。
hint.en: Where does the pasted cover fail to line up? In a book photographed at an angle, the far edge is shorter.

text.zh: 点对 · 封面 → 照片

after.zh: 变形加上一张同样变形的掩膜，就能把一张图合成进另一张：AR 贴图、全景拼接、换天空都是这一步。
after.en: A warp plus a mask warped the same way composites one picture into another: AR overlays, panorama stitching and sky replacement all take this step.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="homography"></part-ref>：点对进去，出来 H 的 9 个数。这一关先不用它，H 直接给你。
t.en: The <part-ref to="homography"></part-ref> in the tray: pairs go in and the 9 numbers of H come out. This level does not need it yet: H is given.

t.zh: 新元件<part-ref to="part:warp"></part-ref>按 H 把一张图搬到另一张图上。
t.en: The new part <part-ref to="part:warp"></part-ref> carries a picture onto another by H.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：把清楚的封面贴到照片里书的位置上。
t.en: Your task in this level: paste the crisp cover over the book in the photo.

brief.zh: 已知把封面搬到照片里的单应 H。把清楚的封面贴到照片里书的位置上：封面落到的地方是封面，其余还是照片。
brief.en: The homography H that carries the cover into the photo is given. Paste the crisp cover over the book in the photo: where the cover lands it is the cover, everywhere else still the photo.

hint.zh: <part-ref to="part:warp"></part-ref>能搬任何一张图。要知道封面落在哪，可以搬一张和封面一样大、全是 1 的图。
hint.en: <part-ref to="part:warp"></part-ref> can carry any picture. To know where the cover lands, carry a picture the size of the cover that is all 1.

after.zh: 匹配、RANSAC 选内点、解单应、变形贴图：这条流水线就是 AR 书封面、全景拼接和文档扫描 App 的核心。每一步你都亲手做过一遍。
after.en: Match, choose inliers with RANSAC, solve the homography, warp and paste: this pipeline is the core of AR book covers, panorama stitching and document-scanning apps, and you have built every step of it yourself.

t.zh: 真实的点对来自匹配器，桌面的花纹一格格重复，难免配错几对。
t.en: Real pairs come from the matcher, and with a desk pattern that repeats tile after tile, a few are bound to be wrong.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：用这些点对把封面贴回照片。
t.en: Your task in this level: paste the cover back onto the photo using these pairs.

brief.zh: 手机斜着拍了桌上的书。匹配器给出了封面和照片之间的点对，其中有几对是桌面花纹造成的错配。把清楚的封面贴回照片里书的位置。
brief.en: A phone photographed the book on the desk at an angle. The matcher has given pairs of points between the cover and the photo, and a few are wrong matches caused by the desk pattern. Paste the crisp cover back over the book in the photo.

hint.zh: 错配只要混进一对，用全部点对解出的 H 就会歪。
hint.en: Let a single wrong match in, and an H solved from all the pairs comes out crooked.

pairs.zh: 匹配的点对（每 4 个数一对）

after.zh: 「等于周围最大值」的格子才是峰顶：这叫非极大值抑制（NMS）。一块 3×3 的最大值可以拆成先横后竖，和可分离的模糊一个道理。
after.en: Only a cell equal to the largest around it is a top: this is called non-maximum suppression (NMS). The maximum over a 3×3 block splits into across then down, just like a separable blur.

t.zh: 响应图一过门槛，留下的是一片一片：一个角附近有好几格都很强。可一个角只该是一个点。
t.en: Above a threshold a response map leaves patches: several cells near one corner are all strong. But a corner should be a single point.

t.zh: 一片里真正的位置是它的峰顶：比四周都高的那一格。
t.en: The true position in a patch is its top: the cell higher than everything around it.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：一张响应图上有几个鼓包，只在峰顶输出 1。
t.en: Your task in this level: a response map has a few bumps; output 1 only at their tops.

desc.zh: 比 3×3 邻居都不小、又大于 0.3 的格子输出 1，其余输出 0。
desc.en: Outputs 1 where a cell is no smaller than its 3×3 neighbours and above 0.3, and 0 elsewhere.

brief.zh: 一张响应图上有几个鼓包。只在峰顶输出 1：这一格比 3×3 邻居都不小，而且大于 0.3。
brief.en: A response map has a few bumps. Output 1 only at the tops: a cell no smaller than any of its 3×3 neighbours, and above 0.3.

hint.zh: 先算出每一格周围 3×3 里最大的是多少。<part-ref to="max"></part-ref>一次只比两张图，可以先横着比、再竖着比。
hint.en: First work out the largest value in the 3×3 around each cell. <part-ref to="max"></part-ref> compares only two pictures at a time, so compare across first, then down.

after.zh: 响应图一过门槛就是一片，片里只有峰顶是真正的角。先算响应、再找峰，是所有检测器的固定套路：角点、直线、物体框都这样。
after.en: Above a threshold the response is a patch, and only its top is the real corner. Response first, then peaks: every detector follows this routine, for corners, lines and object boxes alike.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="own-6-2"></part-ref>在比 3×3 邻居都不小、又大于 0.3 的格子输出 1，其余输出 0。
t.en: The <part-ref to="own-6-2"></part-ref> in the tray outputs 1 where a cell is no smaller than its 3×3 neighbours and above 0.3, and 0 elsewhere.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：每个角只输出一个点。
t.en: Your task in this level: output a single point per corner.

brief.zh: 每个角只输出一个点：Harris 响应乘 2 以后，峰顶输出 1。
brief.en: Output a single point per corner: after multiplying the Harris response by 2, output 1 at its tops.

hint.zh: 门槛只能留下一块一块，每个角留下好几格。
hint.en: A threshold leaves blobs: several cells per corner.

after.zh: 重复的花纹里，第一名和第二名几乎一样近：这种匹配再像也不可信。距离比检验 d₁ / d₂ < 0.8 只接受第一名明显领先的匹配，整体变亮也不影响比值。
after.en: In repeated texture the first and second places are almost equally close: however alike, such a match cannot be trusted. The ratio test d₁ / d₂ < 0.8 accepts only a match whose first place is clearly ahead, and an overall brightening does not change the ratio.

t.zh: 两张图里各有一些好认的点，还要把它们配成对：左图的这个点，是右图的哪一个？最直接的办法是比外观，拿它周围的一小块，到右图里找最像的一块。
t.en: Each image has some points that are easy to recognise, and they still have to be paired up: which point in the right image is this point from the left image? The most direct way is to compare how they look: take a small patch around it and search the right image for the most similar patch.

t.zh: 像不像用距离 d 来量：两块逐格相减、平方、加起来再开方，d 越小越像。每个点在右图里最像的叫第一名，距离 d₁；其次是第二名，距离 d₂。
t.en: Similarity is measured by a distance d: subtract the two patches pixel by pixel, square, add up, then take the square root. The smaller d is, the more alike they are. For each point, the closest match in the right image is first place, at distance d₁; the next is second place, at distance d₂.

t.zh: 这一关把比较的结果直接交给你：每一格是一个关键点，三张图是它到三个候选的距离。最近的不一定可信：要是第二近的几乎一样近，这一对就可能是重复花纹配错了。
t.en: This level hands you the comparisons directly: each cell is a keypoint, and the three maps are its distances to three candidates. The nearest is not always to be trusted: if the second nearest is almost as near, the pair may be a mistake caused by repeated texture.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：按说明里的规则，输出每个关键点配上的候选编号，不可信的输出 0。
t.en: Your task in this level: following the rule in the brief, output the number of the candidate each keypoint matches, and 0 when the match cannot be trusted.

desc.zh: 最近的距离小于第二近的 0.8 倍时，输出最近那个的编号 1–3；否则输出 0。
desc.en: Outputs the number 1–3 of the nearest when its distance is under 0.8 times the second nearest; otherwise 0.

brief.zh: 每一格是一个关键点，三张图是它到三个候选的距离。最近的距离 d₁ 小于第二近 d₂ 的 0.8 倍时，输出最近那个候选的编号 1、2 或 3；否则输出 0。
brief.en: Each cell is a keypoint, and the three maps are its distances to three candidates. When the nearest distance d₁ is less than 0.8 times the second nearest d₂, output the number of the nearest candidate, 1, 2 or 3; otherwise output 0.

hint.zh: 较小的那个 = 两个相加，再减去较大的那个。三个数里第二小的，是哪两个较小值里较大的？
hint.en: The smaller of two = their sum minus the larger. Of three numbers, which is the second smallest: the larger of which two smaller ones?

title.en: Matching through a change of light

after.zh: 先让每个窗口减去自己的平均亮度，整体变亮就不影响距离了；再除以自己的标准差，连对比度变了也不怕。这就是归一化互相关（NCC）的想法，SIFT 描述子也会做类似的归一化。
after.en: Subtract each window's own mean brightness first, and an overall brightening no longer affects the distance; divide by its own standard deviation as well, and even a contrast change does not matter. This is the idea behind normalised cross-correlation (NCC), and SIFT descriptors are normalised in a similar way.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="own-6-4"></part-ref>接上三个距离，它给出配上的候选编号。
t.en: The <part-ref to="own-6-4"></part-ref> in the tray takes three distances and returns the number of the matching candidate.

t.zh: 两张照片常常不是同时拍的，光线变了，同一处在右图里整体亮一截。
t.en: Two photos are often not taken at the same moment: the light changes, and the same place is brighter all over in the right one.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：找出哪个候选窗口和关键点的窗口是同一处，输出它的编号。
t.en: Your task in this level: find which candidate window shows the same place as the keypoint window, and output its number.

brief.zh: 右图整体亮了一截。用匹配器找出哪个候选窗口和关键点的窗口是同一处，输出它的编号。
brief.en: The right image is brighter all over. Use the matcher to find which candidate window shows the same place as the keypoint window, and output its number.

hint.zh: 距离 = 平均((窗口 − 候选)²)。整体亮了一截时，每一格都差同一个数，这一点能先去掉吗？
hint.en: Distance = average((window − candidate)²). When everything is brighter by some amount, every cell differs by the same number. Can you take that away first?

after.zh: Hough 把“找一条线”变成“在累加器里找峰”。分箱太细，噪声把一条线的票拆成许多小峰；太粗，相近的两条线合成一个峰。合适的分箱取决于噪声和线的间距。
after.en: Hough turns "find a line" into "find a peak in the accumulator". With bins too fine, noise splits one line's votes into many small peaks; too coarse, and two nearby lines merge into one peak. The right bin size depends on the noise and on how far apart the lines are.

t.zh: 很多时候要找的是一条线：车道线、纸张的边、楼房的轮廓。边缘检测给的只是一堆零散的点，还夹着噪声和不相干的点。怎样从中认出直线？
t.en: Often what you are looking for is a line: a lane marking, the edge of a sheet of paper, the outline of a building. Edge detection only gives a scatter of loose points, mixed with noise and unrelated points. How do you pick out straight lines from that?

t.zh: Hough 变换让点来投票。一条直线可以用两个数记下：方向 θ，和它离中心的距离 ρ。每个点给所有穿过它的直线投票，真有的那条线会收到很多票。
t.en: The Hough transform lets the points vote. A straight line can be written down with two numbers: its direction θ and its distance ρ from the centre. Every point votes for all the lines passing through it, and a line that is really there collects lots of votes.

t.zh: 票要落进格子里才能数：(θ, ρ) 的平面被切成一格格，这叫分箱。台上右边就是这些格子，颜色越浓票越多，标出的 1、2 是票最多的两个峰。
t.en: Votes can only be counted once they land in cells: the (θ, ρ) plane is cut into a grid, which is called binning. These cells are on the right of the bench; the darker the colour, the more votes, and the marked 1 and 2 are the two peaks with the most votes.

t.zh: 这一关你要调分箱的大小，让三组图里票最多的两个峰正好是那两条线。动手前想想：格子的大小，会影响票怎样聚在一起？
t.en: In this level you tune the bin size so that, in all three sets, the two peaks with the most votes are exactly the two lines. Before you start, think: how does the cell size affect the way votes gather together?

brief.zh: 每个边缘点给所有经过它的直线 (θ, ρ) 各投一票。调分箱大小，让三张图里票数最高的两个峰正好是那两条线。
brief.en: Each edge point casts one vote for every line (θ, ρ) that passes through it. Adjust the bin size so that in all three images the two peaks with the most votes are exactly the two lines.

hint.zh: 格子太细，同一条线带噪声的票落不进同一格；太粗，两条相近的线挤进同一个峰。
hint.en: With cells too fine, one line's noisy votes do not land in the same cell; too coarse, and two nearby lines squeeze into one peak.

text.zh: 目标 · 前两个峰分别匹配 A 和 B
text.en: Goal · the top two peaks match A and B

after.zh: 亮点、投票、找峰：Hough 把「找一条线」变成「在累加器里找峰」，挡掉了零散的杂点，线断了几段也照样找得到。车道保持系统的第一代就是这么做的。
after.en: Points, votes, peaks: Hough turns "find a line" into "find a peak in the accumulator", which ignores scattered specks and still finds a line broken into pieces. The first lane-keeping systems worked exactly like this.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="hough"></part-ref>：亮点进去，出来一张 (θ, ρ) 的票数图。
t.en: The <part-ref to="hough"></part-ref> in the tray: bright points go in, and a map of votes over (θ, ρ) comes out.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：路面上有两条车道线和几个亮点，在累加器里只标出这两条线。
t.en: Your task in this level: the road has two lane lines and a few bright specks; mark only these two lines in the accumulator.

brief.zh: 路面上有两条亮的车道线和几个亮点。在 Hough 累加器里只标出这两条线的格子：票数乘 1/8 以后的峰。
brief.en: The road has two bright lane lines and a few bright specks. Mark only the cells of these two lines in the Hough accumulator: the peaks after multiplying the votes by 1/8.

hint.zh: 每个亮点都投票，可一个孤零零的亮点票数分散，成不了峰。
hint.en: Every bright point votes, but a lone speck spreads its votes thin and makes no peak.

after.zh: 一轮两点都是内点的概率是 p²，k 轮全落空的概率是 (1 − p²)ᵏ。要成功率达到 P，就要 k ≥ log(1 − P) / log(1 − pⁿ)：p = 0.5、n = 2、P = 0.99 时是 17 轮，内点只剩 30% 时要 49 轮。轮数由内点比例决定，δ 由噪声决定，两者不能互相代替。
after.en: The chance that both points of a round are inliers is p², and the chance that all k rounds miss is (1 − p²)ᵏ. To reach a success rate P you need k ≥ log(1 − P) / log(1 − pⁿ): with p = 0.5, n = 2 and P = 0.99 that is 17 rounds, and with only 30% inliers it takes 49. The number of rounds is set by the inlier ratio and δ by the noise; neither can stand in for the other.

t.zh: 配对、找线时总会混进错的点，叫外点；对的点叫内点。用一条线去贴合所有点，几个离得远的外点就能把线拽歪。全景拼接、车道识别都要先对付它们。
t.en: When matching points or finding lines, wrong points always creep in; these are called outliers, and the right ones inliers. If you fit one line to all the points, a few far-off outliers can drag it askew. Panorama stitching and lane detection both have to deal with them first.

t.zh: RANSAC 换了个思路：随机抽两个点连成线，数有多少点离它够近，算作支持；反复抽很多轮，留下支持最多的那条。
t.en: RANSAC takes a different approach: pick two points at random and join them with a line, then count how many points lie close enough to it to count as support. Repeat for many rounds and keep the line with the most support.

caption.zh: RANSAC 钉板：每轮抽两根钉，落在导轨之间的钉投票
caption.en: RANSAC pegboard: each round draws two pegs, and the pegs between the rails vote

t.zh: 台上要定两个数：抽几轮 k，以及离线多近才算支持 δ。每种设置都会跑 200 次试验，看找对的比例。外点比例有三种，每种的轮数都有上限。
t.en: On the bench you set two numbers: the number of rounds k, and δ, how close to the line a point must be to count as support. Each setting is run for 200 trials to see how often it finds the right line. There are three outlier ratios, and each has a cap on the number of rounds.

t.zh: 这一关你要为三种外点比例各选一个 k，再选一个共用的 δ，让成功率都达到 99%。要想的是：外点越多，轮数该怎样变？δ 又该由什么决定？
t.en: In this level you choose a k for each of the three outlier ratios, plus one shared δ, so that every success rate reaches 99%. The questions are: as outliers increase, how should the number of rounds change? And what should decide δ?

brief.zh: 每轮随机抽 2 个点连成直线，数离它不到 δ 的点，k 轮后留下支持最多的一条。三种外点比例下，各用不超过预算的 k，让 200 次试验的成功率都 ≥ 99%。
brief.en: Each round draws 2 random points, joins them into a line and counts the points closer than δ to it; after k rounds the line with the most support is kept. For each of the three outlier ratios, use a k within the budget so that the success rate over 200 trials is ≥ 99%.

hint.zh: 外点越多，一轮抽中两个内点的机会越小。δ 只和噪声有关：太小漏掉真内点，太大把外点也算进来。
hint.en: The more outliers, the smaller the chance that a round draws two inliers. δ depends only on the noise: too small misses true inliers, too large counts outliers in as well.

text.zh: δ 由三种比例共用。色带是与直线距离小于 δ 的范围；虚线是真实直线，圆圈标出抽中的两点
text.en: δ is shared by all three ratios. The band covers everything closer than δ to the line; the dashed line is the true line, and the circled points are the two drawn

title.en: A line that will not be dragged

after.zh: 最小二乘会被每个杂点往外拽一点；RANSAC 只信得到最多支持的那条线，再用它的内点重新拟合，杂点再多也拽不歪。要几轮由杂点的比例决定，δ 由线上点的抖动决定。
after.en: Least squares gets pulled a little by every speck; RANSAC trusts only the line with the most support and refits it on its inliers, so however many specks there are they cannot drag it. The number of rounds is set by the share of specks, and δ by how much the points on the line wobble.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="ransac"></part-ref>，轮数 k 和 δ 都能调。
t.en: The <part-ref to="ransac"></part-ref> in the tray has the rounds k and δ to set.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：边缘图里有一条直线和一堆杂点，把这条线画出来。
t.en: Your task in this level: an edge map holds one straight line and a heap of specks; draw the line.

brief.zh: 边缘图里有一条直线和一堆杂点。画出这条直线（离线不到 0.7 的格子为 1）。
brief.en: An edge map holds one straight line and a heap of specks. Draw the line (cells closer than 0.7 are 1).

hint.zh: 杂点越多，一轮抽中两个线上点的机会越小。
hint.en: The more specks, the smaller the chance that a round draws two points on the line.

after.zh: 形状只在「匹配」里出现：每张图单看都只是杂点。对应点只需在同一行里找，视差越大，物体越近。
after.en: The shape only appears through matching: each image on its own is just speckle. Corresponding points only need to be searched for along the same row, and the larger the disparity, the nearer the object.

t.zh: 伸出一根手指放在眼前，轮流闭上左眼和右眼：手指和远处的墙，哪个跳得更厉害？同一样东西在两只眼里错开的距离，叫视差。
t.en: Hold a finger up in front of your eyes and close your left and right eye in turn: which jumps more, your finger or the far wall? The distance by which the same thing is offset between your two eyes is called disparity.

t.zh: 机器人和汽车上的双目相机也靠视差判断远近。这一关的两张图都是随机噪点，单看哪张都没有形状；心理学家 Julesz 在 1960 年用这种图证明，人不认出任何物体也能看出立体。
t.en: The stereo cameras on robots and cars also use disparity to judge distance. Both images in this level are random dots, and neither shows any shape on its own; in 1960 the psychologist Julesz used images like these to show that people can see depth without recognising any object.

t.zh: 新原件<part-ref to="part:argmin4"></part-ref>接四张图，逐格看哪一张最小，输出它的编号 0–3。
t.en: The new primitive <part-ref to="part:argmin4"></part-ref> takes four pictures and, cell by cell, outputs the number 0–3 of the one that is smallest.

t.zh: 输出是一张视差图：每格填 0 到 3，表示那里的东西在两张图之间错开了几格，少数格子出错可以接受。要想的是：怎样判断右图的某一格和左图的这一格是同一处？
t.en: The output is a disparity map: each pixel holds 0 to 3, the number of pixels by which the thing there is offset between the two images. A few wrong pixels are fine. The question is: how can you tell that a pixel in the right image is the same spot as this pixel in the left image?

caption.zh: 左图、右图 → 每格的视差
caption.en: Left image, right image → disparity at each pixel

brief.zh: 左右两台相机拍同一个场景。输出每个像素的视差 d（0 … 3）：右图里同一个点比左图往左挪了几格。
brief.en: Two cameras, left and right, photograph the same scene. Output each pixel's disparity d (0 … 3): how many pixels further left the same point is in the right image.

hint.zh: 对每个可能的 d，把右图挪一挪再和左图比。单个像素比不准时，看看它周围。
hint.en: For each possible d, shift the right image and compare it with the left one. When single pixels do not compare reliably, look at what is around them.

after.zh: 搜视差、换成距离、只留地面以上：每一步都是前面单独练过的，接起来就是一台测距仪。
after.en: Search the disparity, convert to distance, keep only what is above the floor: each step was practised on its own earlier, and joined up they make a rangefinder.

t.zh: 扫地机器人装了一对双目相机，要在撞上之前停下来。先要知道前面每个地方有多远。
t.en: A robot vacuum has a pair of stereo cameras and must stop before it bumps into things. First it needs to know how far away everything in front is.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：输出地面以上每个像素的距离。
t.en: Your task in this level: output the distance of every pixel above the floor.

brief.zh: 扫地机器人的双目相机（f·b = 3）。输出地面以上每个像素的距离（米），地面那几行输出 0。
brief.en: A robot vacuum's stereo camera (f·b = 3). Output the distance in metres of every pixel above the floor, and 0 on the floor rows.

hint.zh: 前面练过的几步，接起来。
hint.en: The steps you have practised, joined up.

after.zh: 地板本来就在前面，算进来机器人就永远停着；所以只看可能有障碍的区域。真实的避障还会用相机的高度和角度，从深度算出每一点离地多高。
after.en: The floor is always in front, so counting it would keep the robot stopped for ever; only the region where obstacles can be is checked. Real obstacle avoidance also uses the camera's height and angle to work out how high above the floor each point is.

t.zh: 地板没有纹理，算出来的距离在那几行乱跳。机器人只关心地面以上、离得很近的东西。
t.en: The floor has no texture, so the distances worked out on those rows jump about. The robot only cares about things above the floor that are very close.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：标出地面以上、近到要停下的像素。
t.en: Your task in this level: mark the pixels above the floor that are close enough to stop for.

brief.zh: 距离近于 1.2 米、又在地面以上的像素输出 1，其余 0。
brief.en: Output 1 for pixels closer than 1.2 m that are above the floor, otherwise 0.

hint.zh: 阈值留下的是「大于」的那边。
hint.en: A threshold keeps the "greater than" side.

after.zh: 窗口、距离换算、感兴趣区域，一个都不能少：这是一台最简单的双目避障系统。真实的扫地机器人还会结合激光或结构光，补上没有纹理的地方。
after.en: Window, distance conversion, region of interest: none can be left out. This is the simplest stereo obstacle-avoidance system; real robot vacuums also use a laser or structured light to fill in where there is no texture.

t.zh: 把前面几关接起来：从两台相机的画面，一路算到要停下的区域。
t.en: Join the last few levels up: from the two cameras' pictures all the way to the region to stop for.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：标出要停下的区域。
t.en: Your task in this level: mark the region to stop for.

brief.zh: 扫地机器人的双目相机（f·b = 3，地板没有纹理，画面有噪声）。标出地面以上、近于 1.2 米、要停下来的区域。
brief.en: A robot vacuum's stereo camera (f·b = 3, a floor with no texture, a noisy picture). Mark the region above the floor, closer than 1.2 m, where it must stop.

hint.zh: 没有纹理的地方，视差搜索什么也配不上。
hint.en: Where there is no texture, disparity search cannot match anything.

after.zh: 没有对所有图都最好的窗口：大窗口抗噪但抹掉细节，小窗口保细节但怕噪声。很多视觉问题都是这种权衡。
after.en: No window is best for every image: a large window resists noise but wipes out detail; a small one keeps detail but is vulnerable to noise. Many vision problems involve this kind of trade-off.

t.zh: <level-ref to="7-1"></level-ref>搭的匹配，现在打包成了元件<part-ref to="disparity"></part-ref>。它只有一个参数：窗口，也就是比较时围着每格取多大一块，两张图按整块来比。
t.en: The matching you built in <level-ref to="7-1"></level-ref> is now packed into the <part-ref to="disparity"></part-ref> part. It has a single parameter: the window, which is how big a patch to take around each pixel when comparing; the two images are compared patch by patch.

t.zh: 真实的立体相机也要挑这个大小。街景里有大片的墙，也有细细的电线杆和栏杆；光线暗时，照片上满是噪点。同一台相机，要对付所有这些。
t.en: Real stereo cameras have to pick this size too. A street scene has large stretches of wall, but also thin power poles and railings; in dim light the photos are full of noise. The same camera has to cope with all of it.

t.zh: 三组测试：有噪声的方块、一根细柱、一个更近的噪声方块。同一个窗口要三组都算对：和真实视差差不超过 1，错的格子不多。
t.en: Three test sets: a noisy square, a thin pillar, and a closer noisy square. A single window must get all three right: within 1 of the true disparity, with only a few wrong pixels.

caption.zh: 细柱：视差图里也只是一根细柱
caption.en: The thin pillar: in the disparity map it is still just a thin pillar

t.zh: 这一关只给这一个元件，你要定的是窗口。动手前想一想：窗口变大，比较时多得到了什么，又丢掉了什么？
t.en: This level gives you only this one part; what you decide is the window. Before you start, think: when the window grows, what does the comparison gain, and what does it lose?

brief.zh: 用视差搜索元件。噪声图和细柱图都要算对（与真实视差相差不超过 1、错的像素不多）。
brief.en: Use the Disparity search part. Get both the noisy images and the thin-bar image right (within 1 of the true disparity, with few wrong pixels).

hint.zh: 窗口小，噪声会骗过匹配；窗口大，细东西会被周围的背景淹没。
hint.en: With a small window, noise fools the matching; with a large one, thin things drown in the surrounding background.

after.zh: 距离和视差成反比：视差差一格，近处只差几厘米，远处可能差好几米，深度误差约是 z²/(f·b)。要让远处测得准，就要加宽基线或换长焦，可近处的视差又会大得超出搜索范围。
after.en: Distance is inversely proportional to disparity: a one-pixel slip in disparity is a few centimetres up close but can be metres far away, with a depth error of about z²/(f·b). To measure far things precisely you widen the baseline or use a longer lens, but then the disparity of near things grows past the search range.

t.zh: 知道了视差，还要换成米。距离、视差、镜头焦距 f、两台相机的间距 b（叫基线）之间有一个固定的关系，它和小孔成像是同一个道理。
t.en: Once you know the disparity, you still need to turn it into metres. Distance, disparity, the lens focal length f and the spacing b between the two cameras (called the baseline) are tied by a fixed relationship, and it follows from the same idea as the pinhole camera.

t.zh: 机器人靠双目相机躲障碍。视差只能按像素算，差一个像素，报出的距离就差一截；视差太大，又会超出相机能搜索的范围，那就配不上了。
t.en: A robot uses stereo cameras to avoid obstacles. Disparity can only be measured in whole pixels, so being off by one pixel puts the reported distance off by a fair amount; and if the disparity is too large, it falls outside the range the camera can search, so no match is found.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：把视差图换成距离图，公式在说明里。
t.en: Your task in this level: turn the disparity map into a distance map; the formula is in the brief.

brief.zh: 这台双目相机的焦距 × 基线 f·b = 3。把视差图换成距离图：z = f·b / d（米）。
brief.en: This stereo camera's focal length × baseline is f·b = 3. Turn the disparity map into a distance map: z = f·b / d (metres).

hint.zh: 一个常数除以一整张图，常数用在每一格上。
hint.en: A constant divided by a whole picture applies to every cell.

after.zh: 只有乘积 f·b 要紧：焦距翻倍、基线减半，测出来的距离一模一样。挑相机时比的是这个乘积。
after.en: Only the product f·b matters: double the focal length and halve the baseline and the distances come out exactly the same. When choosing a camera, this product is what to compare.

t.zh: 换一台双目相机，镜头和两台相机的间距都变了。
t.en: Switch to a different stereo camera: both the lens and the distance between the two cameras change.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：每组测试给出焦距 f 和基线 b，把视差图换成距离图。
t.en: Your task in this level: each test gives the focal length f and the baseline b; turn the disparity map into a distance map.

brief.zh: 换了一台双目相机，焦距 f 和基线 b 每组测试都不一样。把视差图换成距离图。
brief.en: A different stereo camera: the focal length f and the baseline b change from test to test. Turn the disparity map into a distance map.

hint.zh: <level-ref to="7-3"></level-ref>的 3 是哪两个数相乘来的？
hint.en: Which two numbers multiplied together made <level-ref to="7-3"></level-ref>'s 3?

after.zh: 叉积和两个向量都垂直。在齐次坐标里，一个点 (x, y, 1) 和一条线 (a, b, c) 都是三个数：两点的叉积是过它们的线，两线的叉积是它们的交点。
after.en: The cross product is perpendicular to both vectors. In homogeneous coordinates a point (x, y, 1) and a line (a, b, c) are both three numbers: the cross product of two points is the line through them, and of two lines it is the point where they meet.

t.zh: 接下来几关，一个点、一条线都写成三个数，放在一行里：点 (x, y) 写成 (x, y, 1)，线 ax + by + c = 0 写成 (a, b, c)。这叫齐次坐标。
t.en: In the next few levels a point and a line are both written as three numbers in a row: the point (x, y) as (x, y, 1), and the line ax + by + c = 0 as (a, b, c). These are called homogeneous coordinates.

t.zh: 叉积把两组三个数变成新的三个数，和原来两个都垂直。
t.en: The cross product turns two sets of three numbers into a new three, perpendicular to both.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：按说明里的公式算出 a × b。
t.en: Your task in this level: work out a × b by the formula in the brief.

desc.zh: 输出两个三维向量的叉积 a × b。
desc.en: Outputs the cross product a × b of two 3-vectors.

brief.zh: 输出 a × b：第 i 个数 = a 的第 i+1 个 × b 的第 i+2 个 − a 的第 i+2 个 × b 的第 i+1 个，下标数到头就从第一个接着数。
brief.en: Output a × b: number i = a's number i+1 × b's number i+2 − a's number i+2 × b's number i+1, with the count going round to the first again past the end.

hint.zh: 平移的「边界」设置多了「循环」：挪出去的从另一头回来。
hint.en: Shift's "Border" setting now has "Wrap round": what moves out comes back in at the other end.

after.zh: 两次叉积就找到了交点，不用解方程。三个数 (X, Y, W) 表示点 (X/W, Y/W)；两条线平行时 W = 0，交点在无穷远处，齐次坐标照样写得出来。
after.en: Two cross products find the meeting point with no equations to solve. Three numbers (X, Y, W) stand for the point (X/W, Y/W); when the lines are parallel W = 0 and they meet at infinity, which homogeneous coordinates can still write down.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="own-7-5"></part-ref>输出两个三维向量的叉积 a × b。
t.en: The <part-ref to="own-7-5"></part-ref> in the tray outputs the cross product a × b of two 3-vectors.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：每条线给出它上面的两个点，输出两条线的交点。
t.en: Your task in this level: each line is given by two points on it; output where the two lines meet.

brief.zh: 每个点写成 (x, y, 1)。线一过 p、q，线二过 r、s。输出两条线的交点，也写成三个数（不必把第三个数化成 1）。
brief.en: Each point is written (x, y, 1). Line 1 passes through p and q, line 2 through r and s. Output where the two lines meet, also as three numbers (no need to make the third one 1).

hint.zh: 叉积能从两个点得到一条线。
hint.en: The cross product turns two points into a line.

after.zh: 左图的一个点，在右图里只可能落在一条线上：这条线就是极线 l′ = F·p。匹配时只沿这条线搜，就从整张图缩成了一条线；两台相机平行时，极线正好是同一行，所以之前只在同一行里找。
after.en: A point in the left image can only land on one line in the right image: the epipolar line l′ = F·p. Searching only along it shrinks the search from a whole image to a line; when the two cameras are parallel the epipolar lines are exactly the rows, which is why the search so far stayed within one row.

t.zh: 到这里为止，两台相机都摆得很正，同一点总在同一行，只要左右找。真实的相机很难摆得这么正，稍微一转，同一点就跑到了别的行。
t.en: So far the two cameras have been set up perfectly straight, so the same point was always on the same row and you only had to search left and right. Real cameras are hard to align that well; turn one slightly and the same point moves to a different row.

t.zh: 好在两台相机的相对位置可以事先标定，记成一个 3×3 的矩阵 F，叫基础矩阵。有了它，左图的一个点在右图里不是哪里都可能出现。
t.en: Fortunately the relative position of the two cameras can be calibrated in advance and recorded as a 3×3 matrix F, the fundamental matrix. With it, a point in the left image cannot turn up just anywhere in the right one.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：算出左图一个点在右图对应的那条线 F·p，F 按列给出。
t.en: Your task in this level: work out the line F·p in the right image that corresponds to a point in the left image; F is given column by column.

desc.zh: 读 F 的三列和点 (x, y)，输出极线 F·p。
desc.en: Reads the three columns of F and a point (x, y), and outputs the epipolar line F·p.

brief.zh: 左图的点 p = (x, y, 1)。输出它在右图的极线 l′ = F·p，三个数。F 按列给出。
brief.en: A point in the left image is p = (x, y, 1). Output its epipolar line in the right image, l′ = F·p, three numbers. F is given column by column.

hint.zh: 矩阵乘一个向量，就是把矩阵的列按向量的数加权相加。
hint.en: A matrix times a vector is the matrix's columns added up, weighted by the vector's numbers.

title.en: Is the point on the line?

after.zh: 一个点在线上，当且仅当 q·l′ = qᵀF p = 0：这就是对极约束。它不告诉你配的是哪个点，只排除不可能的点，所以常用来筛掉错配。
after.en: A point lies on the line exactly when q·l′ = qᵀF p = 0: this is the epipolar constraint. It does not say which point is the match, only rules out impossible ones, so it is often used to throw out wrong matches.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="own-7-7"></part-ref>读 F 的三列和点 (x, y)，输出极线 F·p。
t.en: The <part-ref to="own-7-7"></part-ref> in the tray reads the three columns of F and a point (x, y), and outputs the epipolar line F·p.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：判断右图的点 q 能不能和左图的点 p 对应。
t.en: Your task in this level: decide whether the right point q can correspond to the left point p.

brief.zh: 右图的点 q 能和左图的点 p 对应吗？q 落在 p 的极线上（|q·l′| < 0.05）输出 1，否则输出 0。
brief.en: Can the right point q correspond to the left point p? Output 1 if q lies on p's epipolar line (|q·l′| < 0.05), otherwise 0.

hint.zh: 点乘就是逐个相乘再加起来；三个数的平均乘 3 就是它们的和。
hint.en: A dot product multiplies number by number and adds up; the average of three numbers times 3 is their sum.

solution: l = own-7-7(c1, c2, c3, px, py)
naive: l = own-7-7(c1, c2, c3, px, py)

after.zh: 极点是另一台相机的光心在这张图里的位置：所有极线都从它发出。它垂直于 F 的每一列，所以是两列的叉积，也就是 Fᵀe′ = 0 的解。
after.en: The epipole is where the other camera's centre appears in this image: every epipolar line comes out of it. It is perpendicular to every column of F, so it is the cross product of two columns: the solution of Fᵀe′ = 0.

t.zh: 左图里不同的点，在右图里有不同的极线。把它们都画出来，会发现一件事：它们都交于同一点。
t.en: Different points in the left image have different epipolar lines in the right image. Draw them all and you notice something: they all pass through one point.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：只用 F 算出这一点，写成 (x, y, 1)。
t.en: Your task in this level: work this point out from F alone, written as (x, y, 1).

brief.zh: 右图里所有的极线都交于同一点，叫极点。只用 F 算出它，写成 (x, y, 1)。
brief.en: In the right image every epipolar line passes through one point, the epipole. Work it out from F alone, written as (x, y, 1).

hint.zh: 每条极线都是 F 的列的组合。两条极线交在哪里，你会算。
hint.en: Every epipolar line is a mix of the columns of F. You know how to find where two lines meet.

title.en: Two numbers to remember an image

after.zh: 编码器把图压成 z，解码器再从 z 画回来，目标就是输入自己，不需要标签。最窄的那层叫瓶颈：这一族斑点只在左右、上下两个方向变，所以瓶颈至少要两个数；一个数只能让斑点沿一条直线走。
after.en: The encoder squeezes the image into z, and the decoder draws it back from z; the target is the input itself, so no labels are needed. The narrowest layer is called the bottleneck: this family of blobs varies only left–right and up–down, so the bottleneck needs at least two numbers; one number can only move the blob along a straight line.

t.zh: 这一章要让机器画出没见过的图。第一步是学会用很少的数描述一张图。一张 16×16 的图有 256 个数；如果这些图都只是同一个斑点换了位置，真的要 256 个数吗？
t.en: This chapter teaches a machine to draw images it has never seen. The first step is learning to describe an image with very few numbers. A 16×16 image has 256 numbers; if all the images are just the same blob in different places, do you really need 256?

t.zh: 新元件<part-ref to="part:dg_encode"></part-ref>把整张图压成一行几个数，<part-ref to="part:dg_decode"></part-ref>再由这几个数画回一张图。中间这几个数就像寄信只写地址，不用附上整栋房子的照片。
t.en: The new <part-ref to="part:dg_encode"></part-ref> part squeezes the whole image into a short row of numbers, and the <part-ref to="part:dg_decode"></part-ref> draws an image back from those numbers. The few numbers in the middle are like writing just the address on a letter, with no need to enclose a photo of the whole house.

t.zh: 两个元件的权重都靠训练：按下训练，机器自己一点点调。编码器可以选压成 1、2 或 3 个数。压缩、去噪都从这一步开始。
t.en: Both parts get their weights from training: press Train and the machine adjusts them bit by bit on its own. You can choose whether the encoder squeezes to 1, 2 or 3 numbers. Compression and denoising both start from this step.

t.zh: 测试是十六个位置不同的斑点，期望输出和输入一模一样。用的数越少越好，所以要找的是：最少几个数还够用？
t.en: The tests are sixteen blobs in different positions, and the expected output is identical to the input. The fewer numbers you use the better, so what you are looking for is: what is the smallest number that still works?

caption.zh: 斑点进去，同一个斑点出来
caption.en: A blob goes in, the same blob comes out

brief.zh: 先把图压成几个数，再由这几个数画回原图。用最少的数做到。
brief.en: Squeeze the image into a few numbers, then draw the original back from those numbers. Do it with as few numbers as you can.

hint.zh: 一个数只能让斑点沿一条线走。这些斑点在往几个方向变？
hint.en: One number can only move the blob along a line. In how many directions do these blobs vary?

after.zh: 只要知道噪声，原图一步就能还原。扩散模型要学的正是这件事：看着 x_t 猜出 ε。猜得越准，还原得越好。
after.en: Know the noise and the original comes back in one step. This is exactly what a diffusion model learns: looking at x_t, guess ε. The better the guess, the better the restoration.

t.zh: 加噪是往前走。生成一张图要往回走：从噪声里把图找回来。
t.en: Adding noise goes forwards. Generating a picture goes backwards: finding the picture again in the noise.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：知道当初加的是哪份噪声，把原图还原出来。
t.en: Your task in this level: knowing which noise was added, get the original picture back.

desc.zh: 输出 (x_t − √(1 − ᾱ)·ε) / √ᾱ：由 x_t 和噪声 ε 还原 x₀。
desc.en: Outputs (x_t − √(1 − ᾱ)·ε) / √ᾱ: x₀ recovered from x_t and the noise ε.

brief.zh: 知道当初加的是哪份噪声 ε，把原图 x₀ 还原出来。
brief.en: Knowing which noise ε was added, get the original picture x₀ back.

hint.zh: 把加噪的公式倒过来解 x₀。
hint.en: Solve the noise formula backwards for x₀.

eps.en: The noise ε that was added

after.zh: 你训练的 3×3 核学会了「和邻居差得多的是噪声」，还原以后笔画就清楚了。扩散模型的去噪网络大得多，从纯噪声出发一步步猜噪声、去掉一点，最后画出一张没见过的图：每一步做的都是这一关的事。
after.en: The 3×3 kernel you trained learnt that "what differs a lot from its neighbours is noise", and after restoring, the strokes are clear. A diffusion model's denoising network is far bigger: starting from pure noise it guesses the noise and removes a little, step after step, until a picture never seen before appears. Every step does what this level does.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="own-8-10"></part-ref>由 x_t 和噪声 ε 还原 x₀。可真要用的时候，没人告诉你噪声是什么。
t.en: The <part-ref to="own-8-10"></part-ref> in the tray recovers x₀ from x_t and the noise ε. But when it is actually needed, nobody tells you what the noise was.

t.zh: <part-ref to="part:learn3"></part-ref>可以训练：按训练，它自己调权重。
t.en: <part-ref to="part:learn3"></part-ref> can be trained: press Train and it adjusts its own weights.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：修好一张满是噪点的旧照片，再标出字的笔画。
t.en: Your task in this level: mend an old photo full of grain, then mark the strokes of the letter.

brief.zh: 一张印着字母的旧照片，满是噪点（ᾱ = 0.9）。这次不知道噪声是什么：训练一个元件从照片里猜出噪声，还原照片，再标出字的笔画。
brief.en: An old photo of a letter, full of grain (ᾱ = 0.9). This time the noise is unknown: train a part to guess the noise from the photo, restore the photo, then mark the strokes of the letter.

hint.zh: 噪声每一格都不一样，字的笔画却连成一片。一格和它的邻居差得多，多半是噪声。
hint.en: The noise differs from cell to cell, but the strokes of a letter join up. A cell very different from its neighbours is probably noise.

after.zh: 像素空间里的中间是两张图叠在一起；潜空间里的中间才是「一个斑点在中间」。训练好的编码器把图放进一个平滑的空间，在里面走直线，解码出来就是一串自然的过渡：人脸变老、换发型都是这么做的。
after.en: Halfway in pixel space is two pictures laid over each other; halfway in latent space is "one blob in between". A trained encoder puts pictures into a smooth space, and walking a straight line there decodes into a natural transition: making a face older or changing a hairstyle works like this.

t.zh: 托盘里有训练好的编码器和解码器：编码器把一个斑点变成两个数，解码器把两个数画成斑点。
t.en: The tray holds the trained encoder and decoder: the encoder turns a blob into two numbers, and the decoder draws two numbers as a blob.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：画出从斑点 a 往斑点 b 走了 t 的那个斑点。
t.en: Your task in this level: draw the blob that is t of the way from blob a to blob b.

brief.zh: 画出 a 和 b 「中间」的那个斑点：从 a 往 b 走了 t（0 是 a，1 是 b）。
brief.en: Draw the blob "between" a and b: t of the way from a to b (0 is a, 1 is b).

hint.zh: 两张图逐格按比例混合，得到的是两个淡斑点。<level-ref to="8-1"></level-ref>的两个数呢？
hint.en: Mixing the two pictures cell by cell gives two faint blobs. What about <level-ref to="8-1"></level-ref>'s two numbers?

t.zh: 走到哪 t
t.en: How far t

after.zh: 瓶颈里只有两个数，装得下「斑点在哪」，装不下每一格的噪声，所以解码出来是干净的。训练时输入加噪声、目标用原图，就是去噪自编码器；后面的扩散模型把这个想法推到底：从纯噪声一点点去噪，画出新图。
after.en: The bottleneck holds only two numbers: enough for "where the blob is", not for the noise in every cell, so what is decoded comes out clean. Training with noisy inputs and the original as the target gives a denoising autoencoder, and diffusion models push the idea all the way: denoise from pure noise, little by little, to draw new pictures.

t.zh: 拍出来的照片总带着噪点。一张图压成两个数，再画回来，噪点会怎样？
t.en: Photos always come with grain. Squeeze a picture into two numbers and draw it back: what happens to the grain?

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：输入的斑点带着噪声，输出干净的斑点。
t.en: Your task in this level: the blobs come in noisy; output clean blobs.

brief.zh: 输入的斑点带着噪声，期望是干净的斑点。
brief.en: The blobs come in noisy, and the expected output is the clean blob.

hint.zh: 模糊把噪声和斑点一起抹开。瓶颈只放得下两个数，噪声要几个数才记得住？
hint.en: A blur smears the noise and the blob alike. The bottleneck holds only two numbers; how many would it take to remember the noise?

after.zh: 采样这一步没法求导：每次重抽，训练分不清结果变好是因为改了 μ、σ 还是运气。把它写成 z = μ + σ·ε，随机全部来自输入 ε，z 对 μ、σ 就只是乘和加，梯度清清楚楚。这叫重参数化，VAE 的编码器就是这样训练的。
after.en: You cannot differentiate through the sampling step: with a fresh draw each time, training cannot tell whether a better result came from changing μ and σ or from luck. Write it as z = μ + σ·ε instead: all the randomness comes from the input ε, z is just a multiply and an add of μ and σ, and the gradient is perfectly clear. This is called reparameterization, and it is how a VAE's encoder is trained.

t.zh: <level-ref to="8-1"></level-ref>的解码器能把两个数画成斑点。要是这两个数随机抽，就能画出没见过的斑点，这就是生成。随机不是乱来：数从正态分布里抽，大多落在中心 μ 附近，σ 越大越散。
t.en: The decoder from <level-ref to="8-1"></level-ref> can turn two numbers into a blob. If those two numbers are drawn at random, it can draw blobs it has never seen: that is generation. Random does not mean anything goes: the numbers are drawn from a normal distribution, so most land near the centre μ, and the larger σ is, the more they spread out.

t.zh: 训练就是把参数拧一点，看结果变好还是变坏，再往好的方向调；能算出该往哪拧，叫求导。可 μ、σ 和画出的图之间夹着一步随机抽样，这种调法还行得通吗？
t.en: Training means nudging the parameters a little, seeing whether the result gets better or worse, and adjusting in the better direction; working out which way to nudge is called differentiating. But there is a random sampling step between μ, σ and the image that gets drawn. Can this kind of adjustment still work?

t.zh: 这一关的元件：μ、σ 各是两个可训练的数；「采样」每算一次都抽一个新的随机数；<part-ref to="dg-decoder"></part-ref>把两个数画成斑点，一个管左右，一个管上下。
t.en: The parts in this level: μ and σ are each two trainable numbers; "Sample" draws a fresh random number every time it runs; <part-ref to="dg-decoder"></part-ref> turns two numbers into a blob, one controlling left-right and the other up-down.

t.zh: 老师画每张图用的随机数 ε，测试都给了你。你要学出老师的 μ 和 σ，用同样的 ε 画出同样的斑点。Stable Diffusion 里压缩、还原图的部分，训练时也要过这一关。
t.en: The tests give you the random numbers ε the teacher used to draw each image. You must learn the teacher's μ and σ so that the same ε draws the same blob. The part of Stable Diffusion that compresses and restores images has to clear this same hurdle in training.

caption.zh: 一组噪声 ε → 老师用它画出的斑点
caption.en: A set of noise ε → the blob the teacher drew with it

brief.zh: 老师用每组的噪声 ε 画出了右边的斑点（z 从 N(μ, σ²) 中采样）。学出 μ 和 σ，用同样的 ε 画出同样的图。
brief.en: The teacher drew the blob on the right from each set's noise ε (z sampled from N(μ, σ²)). Learn μ and σ, and draw the same image from the same ε.

hint.zh: 采样器每算一次都换一个随机数，训练看到的只是噪声。老师用的那组 ε 就在输入里。
hint.en: The sampler draws a new random number every time it runs, so all training sees is noise. The teacher's ε is right there in the input.

after.zh: 训练好以后，生成就是：抽一个随机的 z，交给解码器。每抽一次就是一张没见过的新图；μ、σ 决定新图大概长在哪一带。
after.en: Once trained, generating is just: draw a random z and hand it to the decoder. Each draw is a new picture never seen before; μ and σ decide roughly where the new pictures fall.

t.zh: 托盘里的「重参数化」：μ、σ、ε 进去，出来 μ + σ·ε。
t.en: The Reparameterization in the tray: μ, σ and ε go in, μ + σ·ε comes out.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：用输入的 μ、σ 和噪声 ε 抽一个 z，画出它的斑点。
t.en: Your task in this level: draw a z from the μ, σ and noise ε in the input, and draw its blob.

brief.zh: 从 N(μ, σ²) 里抽一个 z，交给解码器画出来。抽样用输入里的噪声 ε。
brief.en: Draw a z from N(μ, σ²) and hand it to the decoder. Use the noise ε from the input to draw it.

hint.zh: <level-ref to="8-4"></level-ref>最后得到的元件，正好是「用 ε 抽样」。
hint.en: The part you got at the end of <level-ref to="8-4"></level-ref> is exactly "draw a sample using ε".

after.zh: 鉴定员不动、生成器猛练，生成器就把所有样本都放到鉴定员最相信的那一点：两支笔重合，只画一堆，这就是模式坍塌；鉴定员一反应，它们又一起跳到另一堆。让鉴定员跟上、生成器小步走，两支笔才会各占一堆，最后鉴定员的准确率回到 50%。
after.en: If the judge stands still while the generator trains hard, the generator puts every sample on the one spot the judge trusts most: the two pens merge and draw only one cluster. This is mode collapse; as soon as the judge reacts, they jump together to the other cluster. Let the judge keep up and the generator take small steps, and the pens settle on one cluster each, until the judge's accuracy is back to 50%.

t.zh: 另一种生成办法是让两个模型对练：生成器画假样本，鉴定员判断真假。鉴定员越会认，生成器就得画得越像。这叫生成对抗网络（GAN），网上那些「不存在的人脸」就是这样画的。
t.en: Another way to generate is to have two models spar: a generator draws fake samples and a judge decides which are real. The better the judge gets at telling, the more convincing the generator has to be. This is called a generative adversarial network (GAN), and the "faces of people who don't exist" you see online are drawn this way.

t.zh: 台上的真实数据是两堆点。生成器有两支笔，每支在一处落笔。鉴定员是一条曲线 D(x)：越高的地方，它越相信那里的点是真的。
t.en: The real data on the bench is two clusters of points. The generator has two pens, each drawing in one spot. The judge is a curve D(x): the higher it is, the more the judge believes a point there is real.

t.zh: 两边轮流训练。你能定每回合鉴定员练几步、生成器练几步，以及生成器每步走多远。
t.en: The two sides train in turns. You decide how many steps the judge trains each round, how many the generator trains, and how far the generator moves with each step.

t.zh: 这一关要让两堆都画到，鉴定员只能瞎猜，准确率回到一半。动手前想想：两边谁练得多、谁走得快，会带来什么不同？
t.en: In this level both clusters must be drawn, leaving the judge only able to guess, with its accuracy back at one half. Before you start, think: what difference does it make which side trains more, and which moves faster?

brief.zh: 生成器有两支笔，要画出和真实数据一样的两堆点。轮流训练鉴定员和生成器，直到两堆都画到、鉴定员只能瞎猜。
brief.en: The generator has two pens and must draw two clusters of points just like the real data. Take turns training the judge and the generator until both clusters are covered and the judge can only guess.

hint.zh: 生成器一回合走太远，就会一起冲向鉴定员此刻最相信的那一处。
hint.en: If the generator moves too far in one round, both pens rush together to the spot the judge trusts most right now.

text.zh: 目标 · 同时满足，连续 3 回合
text.en: Goals · all at once, 3 rounds in a row

title.zh: 一步加到第 t 步

after.zh: ᾱ 从 1 慢慢减到 0，图一点点没进噪声里。两个系数的平方加起来是 1，所以不管加到哪一步，图的总「能量」大致不变。这个公式让训练时能直接跳到任意一步，不用一步步加。
after.en: As ᾱ falls slowly from 1 to 0, the picture sinks little by little into the noise. The squares of the two coefficients add up to 1, so whatever the step, the total "energy" of the picture stays about the same. This formula lets training jump straight to any step without adding noise step by step.

t.zh: 现在最好的图像生成模型叫扩散模型。它的训练从反方向开始：先把一张图一点点加噪，直到只剩噪声。
t.en: The best image generators today are called diffusion models. Their training starts the other way round: noise is added to a picture little by little until only noise is left.

t.zh: 加到哪一步，用一个数 ᾱ 表示图还剩多少：1 是原图，0 是纯噪声。
t.en: How far it has gone is given by one number, ᾱ, how much of the picture is left: 1 is the original, 0 is pure noise.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：按说明里的公式，一步算出加到第 t 步的图。
t.en: Your task in this level: by the formula in the brief, work out in one step the picture after noise is added up to step t.

desc.zh: 输出 √ᾱ·x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ)·ε：把 x₀ 一步加噪到第 t 步。
desc.en: Outputs √ᾱ·x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ)·ε: x₀ noised straight to step t.

brief.zh: 扩散模型给图加噪：x_t = √ᾱ · x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ) · ε。按公式输出 x_t。
brief.en: A diffusion model adds noise to a picture: x_t = √ᾱ · x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ) · ε. Output x_t by the formula.

hint.zh: √ᾱ 和 √(1 − ᾱ) 都是一个数，乘到整张图上。
hint.en: √ᾱ and √(1 − ᾱ) are each a single number, multiplied onto the whole picture.

after.zh: 展开以后，x₀ 前面的系数是 √(a1·a2)，两份噪声合起来正好是方差 1 − a1·a2 的一份噪声：两次加噪，和按 ᾱ = a1·a2 一次加噪是同一回事。所以扩散的每一步都能一步跳到。
after.en: Expand it and the coefficient of x₀ is √(a1·a2), while the two noises together are exactly one noise of variance 1 − a1·a2: adding noise twice is the same thing as adding it once with ᾱ = a1·a2. That is why any step of diffusion can be reached in one jump.

t.zh: 托盘里的<part-ref to="own-8-7"></part-ref>把 x₀ 一步加噪到第 t 步：输出 √ᾱ·x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ)·ε。
t.en: The <part-ref to="own-8-7"></part-ref> in the tray takes x₀ straight to step t: it outputs √ᾱ·x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ)·ε.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：加两次噪，输出加完两次的图。
t.en: Your task in this level: add noise twice and output the picture after both.

brief.zh: 先按 a1 加一次噪，再对结果按 a2 加一次噪。输出加了两次以后的图。
brief.en: Add noise once with a1, then add noise to the result again with a2. Output the picture after both.

hint.zh: <level-ref to="8-7"></level-ref>的<part-ref to="own-8-7"></part-ref>接两次。
hint.en: <level-ref to="8-7"></level-ref>'s <part-ref to="own-8-7"></part-ref>, twice.

title.en: Draw it on the side asked for

after.zh: 多给生成器一个条件输入，它就按要求画：这叫条件生成。「画一只猫」「画成水彩风格」这些文字提示，就是更复杂的条件。
after.en: Give the generator one more input, a condition, and it draws what is asked for: this is called conditional generation. Text prompts like "draw a cat" or "in watercolour" are just more elaborate conditions.

t.zh: 生成器画出来的东西是随机的。要让它按要求画，得多告诉它一点什么。
t.en: What a generator draws is random. To make it draw what is asked for, it has to be told something more.

t.zh: 这一关你要做的：c = 0 时在左边那一带画斑点，c = 1 时在右边。
t.en: Your task in this level: when c = 0, draw the blob in the region on the left; when c = 1, on the right.

brief.zh: c = 0 时，从左边那一带抽一个斑点；c = 1 时，从右边那一带抽。
brief.en: When c = 0, draw a blob from the region on the left; when c = 1, from the region on the right.

hint.zh: 同样的抽样，只是中心换了。中心能不能由 c 算出来？
hint.en: The same sampling, only with a different centre. Can the centre be worked out from c?

c.zh: 画哪边 c（0 左，1 右）

after.zh: 先补零放大、再用一个核走一遍，就是步幅为 2 的转置卷积：核决定空出来的格子从哪些邻居、按什么比例取数。分割网络的解码器靠它把小特征图一层层放大回原图大小。
after.en: Zero-upsample first, then run a kernel over it: that is a transposed convolution with stride 2, and the kernel decides which neighbours, in what proportion, fill the empty cells.
